P0B00.d: P0B00 is the general fault for phase U of the three-phase motor that drives the electric auxiliary transmission fluid pump, the pump that keeps line pressure while the engine is stopped. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.

Engine auto-stop disabled or no electric drive mode
Delayed engagement or harsh restart after a stop
c: Loose, corroded or unlatched phase U connection at the pump motor
Current sensing in the pump inverter faulty (shunt or phase sensor)
Power stage of phase U in the pump control module faulty
Winding fault in phase U of the pump motor

P0B01.d: P0B01 means the pump inverter sees almost no current in phase U of the auxiliary fluid pump motor, typically an open phase. GM documents the check for the Volt motor control processor (2016) and its hybrid tables of 2018 and 2019: with the drive state in Run, the inverter in normal PWM above 50 V and a squared current command above 5 A2 (2016) or 14.97 A2 (2018), the peak current on the U axis is compared while the r
s: Service Vehicle Soon light and MIL
Propulsion Power Reduced or Vehicle Speed Limited message
c: Pump motor connector not fully seated or latched (Chevrolet Spark EV)
Open circuit in the phase U lead or terminal of the pump motor cable
Phase U switch in the pump inverter not conducting
Open winding of phase U in the pump motor

P0B02.d: P0B02 reports excessive current in phase U of the auxiliary transmission fluid pump motor, an overcurrent condition that the pump inverter must cut off to protect its switches. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.
s: MIL and transmission or hybrid warning
Auxiliary pump shuts down, auto-stop disabled
Harsh or delayed engagement after an engine stop
c: Phase U lead shorted to another phase or to ground
Pump binding mechanically, raising motor current
Current sensing in the pump inverter reads too high
Shorted turns in phase U of the pump motor

P0B03.d: P0B03 covers a general current fault in phase V of the brushless motor of the electric auxiliary transmission fluid pump. No manufacturer publicly describes a monitor for it.
s: MIL or transmission/hybrid warning
Engine auto-stop or electric mode no longer available
c: Poor contact in the phase V lead or pump connector
Current sensing in the pump inverter faulty
Phase V power stage in the pump control module faulty
Winding fault in phase V of the pump motor

P0B04.d: P0B04 indicates that phase V of the auxiliary fluid pump motor carries too little current, usually because the phase is open somewhere between inverter and winding. GM tests it on the Volt (2016) and in the 2018 and 2019 hybrid tables like its U and W siblings: in Run, with normal PWM, more than 50 V on the inverter and a minimum squared current command, the V current is sampled while the rotor sits within 30 degrees
s: Service Vehicle Soon light and MIL
Reduced propulsion power or limited vehicle speed
c: Pump motor connector not fully seated or latched (Chevrolet Spark EV)
Open circuit in the phase V lead or terminal
Phase V switch in the pump inverter not conducting
Open winding of phase V in the pump motor

P0B05.d: P0B05 flags overcurrent in phase V of the electric auxiliary transmission fluid pump motor. No manufacturer publicly documents this specific code.
s: MIL and transmission or hybrid warning
Loss of propulsion or no-start in severe cases
c: Phase V lead shorted to another phase or to ground
Pump seized or contaminated, motor draws excess current
Pump restart logic in the inverter software causing overcurrent
Shorted turns in phase V of the pump motor

P0B06.d: P0B06 is the general current fault for phase W of the auxiliary transmission fluid pump motor. No manufacturer publishes a monitor description for this exact code.
s: MIL or transmission/hybrid warning
Engine keeps running at stops, no auto-stop
c: Poor contact in the phase W lead or pump connector
Current sensing in the pump inverter faulty
Phase W power stage in the pump control module faulty
Winding fault in phase W of the pump motor

P0B07.d: P0B07 means phase W of the auxiliary fluid pump motor carries less current than commanded, the typical sign of an open W path. GM uses it on the Volt and later hybrids: below 1 A peak W-axis current for 0.4 s of 0.6 s, with the inverter in normal PWM above 50 V, sets a Type A fault.
s: MIL and Service Vehicle Soon light
Loss of propulsion, vehicle shutdown or no-start
c: Pump motor connector not fully seated or latched (Chevrolet Spark EV)
Open circuit in the phase W lead or terminal
Outdated inverter software (Cadillac CT6 plug-in, service update 18199)
Open winding of phase W in the pump motor

P0B08.d: P0B08 is set when the current in phase W of the auxiliary transmission fluid pump motor rises above the permitted limit. No manufacturer documents this exact code in public sources.
s: MIL and transmission or hybrid warning
Auxiliary pump shuts down, auto-stop disabled
c: Phase W lead shorted to another phase or to ground
Pump binding mechanically, raising motor current
Current sensing in the pump inverter reads too high
Shorted turns in phase W of the pump motor

P0B09.d: P0B09 concerns the power feed of auxiliary pump A's motor: the controller sees no valid supply voltage, usually because the circuit is open. GM documents it for its 2012-13 eAssist mild hybrids (BAS Plus): the hardware input reports an out-of-range voltage flag on the auxiliary pump circuit, enabled with ignition voltage above 9 V; failing for at least 0.375 s within a 1.2 s sample sets P0B09 as Type B, MIL after two
s: Engine auto-stop no longer occurs
MIL after two drive cycles
Shift flare or delayed drive engagement on restart
c: Blown fuse or open relay in the pump supply
Open supply wire or loose terminal at the pump connector
Poor ground connection of the pump motor
Voltage sensing input in the controller faulty

P0B0A.d: P0B0A means the supply voltage measured at the motor of auxiliary pump A is lower than expected while the pump should be running. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; GM's eAssist tables only cover the open-circuit case as P0B09.
s: Start-stop function inactive
MIL or transmission warning
Jerky drive-off after an engine stop
c: Corroded terminal or high resistance in the pump feed or ground
Weak 12 V battery or poor charging
DC/DC converter or alternator output too low (hybrid)
Voltage sensing input in the controller faulty

P0B0B.d: P0B0B reports a supply voltage at the motor of auxiliary pump A that is above the expected range. Subaru documents it on the 2014-15 XV Crosstrek Hybrid (bulletin 16-94-15R), together with P172A: a leaking O-ring at the electric oil pump relief valve can let CVT fluid into the pump motor.
s: Warning lamp on, hybrid or CVT function restricted
Possibly P0C79 stored at the same time
c: CVT fluid entering the pump motor via a leaking relief valve O-ring (Subaru XV Crosstrek Hybrid)
Supply circuit shorted to a higher voltage source
Oil pump inverter or its voltage sensing faulty

P0B0C.d: P0B0C says the circuit fed by auxiliary pump A loses pressure through a leak, so the pump cannot hold the demanded pressure. Stellantis documents it as P0B0C 7A for the 2023-26 Jeep Avenger and 2026 Compass with hybrid dual-clutch transmission outside the US (TSB 21-061-26): an internal leak at the parking pawl locking piston causes jerking and power loss and may stop the engine from restarting after a stop; with P07
s: Jerking and loss of power while driving
Engine fails to restart after a stop
Transmission warning, possibly with P07E4 or P07E6
c: Internal leak at the parking pawl locking piston (Jeep Avenger/Compass hybrid DCT)
Worn seal or valve leaking inside the hydraulic circuit
External leak and low transmission fluid level
Internal wear of the auxiliary pump

P0B0D.d: P0B0D is an internal fault of the module that drives the auxiliary pump motor. GM documents it for the auxiliary transmission pump controller (ATPC) in its 2011 and 2014 hybrid tables and for the 2016 Cadillac ELR: it checks processor integrity, such as SPI hardware faults or a wrong seed and key between processors, with more than 9.5 V supply; 28 failures out of 32 samples in a 6.25 ms loop, detected within about 20
s: MIL on
Transmission in limp mode
Possibly lost communication with the pump module (U0287)
c: Electric pump with integrated control electronics failed (Jeep 4xe 8P75PH)
Processor or memory fault inside the pump control module
Supply voltage dips or poor ground at the module

P0B0E.d: Many packs measure current with two channels or two sensors so the controller can cross-check them; sensor B is the second channel next to sensor A (P0ABF to P0AC3). P0B0E is its general circuit code.
s: MIL and hybrid system warning on
Battery power limited, less electric assist
Implausible state-of-charge display
c: Signal or ground wire of channel B damaged or connector loose
Current sensor or junction block with integrated sensor defective

P0B0F.d: P0B0F flags a current sensor B signal that is electrically in range but implausible, for example an offset at zero current or a value that does not match the other measurement. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.
s: Hybrid or EV warning, MIL possible
State of charge jumps or drifts
Reduced battery power
c: Current sensor B offset drift or ageing
Ground offset or high resistance in the sensor wiring
Sensor displaced on the busbar or magnetic interference

P0B10.d: P0B10 means the output of current sensor B lies below its valid range. GM uses a dual-range Hall sensor whose channel B covers small currents with high resolution: the 2019 battery energy control module table sets P0B10 when this fine current reads below -24 A (ADC count under 82) for 1.6 s within a 2 s window, Type A, one trip; the 2011 Volt table uses -23 A for 175 ms within 250 ms, one trip.
s: MIL and hybrid system warning on
Battery charge and discharge power limited
Engine runs more often, fuel use rises
c: Sensor B signal line shorted to ground
5 V supply of the current sensor missing
Current sensor or junction block with integrated sensor defective

P0B11.d: P0B11 is set when current sensor B delivers a signal above its valid range. In GM's dual-range design, channel B is the fine channel for small currents: the 2019 battery energy control module table fails it above +24 A (ADC count over 4013) for 1.6 s within a 2 s window, Type A, one trip, and the 2011 Volt table above +23 A for 175 ms within 250 ms, one trip.
s: MIL and hybrid system warning on
Battery power limited, less electric driving
Implausible state-of-charge display
c: Open signal or ground wire of sensor B
Signal line shorted to the sensor supply or 12 V
Current sensor or junction block with integrated sensor defective

P0B12.d: P0B12 covers a current sensor B signal that jumps or drops out in a way real current cannot, typically from a loose connector, a chafed signal wire or noise on the sensor ground. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.
s: Intermittent hybrid or EV warning
Short power reductions during dropouts
Code stored without lasting symptoms
c: Loose connector or poor terminal contact at the current sensor
Electrical noise on the sensor ground

P0B13.d: P0B13 compares the two pack current readings, sensor A and sensor B, and sets when they disagree. On the Chevrolet Volt GM pairs a coarse and a fine channel: the code fails when they differ by more than 10 A while both read between -20 and 20 A, for example 10 s within a 12.5 s window (2016) or 400 of 500 samples at 25 ms (2019), Type A, one trip.
s: MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Red battery or Service High Voltage message, request to stop safely
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist
Charging interrupted or refused
c: Battery controller software fault, fixed by update (Audi, GM)
Disturbance from an external charging station during charging
Offset drift of one of the two current channels
Internal communication fault between switching unit and current sensor

P0B14.d: SAE J2012 reserves up to four pack voltage measurements, A to D; voltage sense B is the second one. P0B14 is its general circuit code: the battery controller sees an electrical fault on this input, typically an open or implausible raw signal.
s: MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist
Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system
c: Voltage sense lead or its fuse open inside the pack
Sense connector at the battery controller loose or corroded
Measurement input of the battery controller defective

P0B15.d: P0B15 marks pack voltage measurement B as electrically valid but implausible: the value lies within the sensor range yet does not match a reference, typically the sum of the cell voltages or another pack measurement. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist
Implausible state-of-charge or range display
c: Drift or calibration error of measurement channel B
Faulty cell voltage acquisition distorts the reference sum
Increased contact resistance at sense terminals
Battery controller software needs an update

P0B16.d: P0B16 sets when pack voltage measurement B reports a value below its plausible minimum, usually an electrical cause such as a sense lead shorted to ground or an open input that pulls the reading down. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist
c: Sense lead of channel B shorted to ground
Fuse or resistor in the sense path open
Measurement input of the battery controller defective

P0B17.d: P0B17 means pack voltage measurement B reads above its plausible maximum. Mercedes-Benz uses this exact code on the eSprinter 907: inaccurate BMS measurements can store P0B171C, voltage sensor B in the high-voltage battery module shorted to positive with the value out of range, together with P0ABD00 for sensor A.
s: Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system
MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist
c: BMS measurement inaccuracy, fixed by software update (Mercedes eSprinter)
Sense lead of channel B shorted to a higher potential
Measurement input of the battery controller defective

P0B18.d: P0B18 reports that pack voltage measurement B jumps or drops out briefly instead of failing steadily. The controller detects implausibly fast changes or short signal losses that disappear again, so the fault often shows up as a history code.
s: Warning appears and disappears, often stored as history
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist
Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system

P0B19.d: Voltage sense C is the third of up to four pack voltage measurements defined in SAE J2012. P0B19 is its general circuit code and sets when the battery controller finds this input electrically unusable, for instance open or without a valid raw value.
s: MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist
Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system
c: Voltage sense lead C or its fuse open
Measurement input of the battery controller defective

P0B1A.d: P0B1A flags pack voltage measurement C as in range but not believable. The controller compares it with a reference, usually the sum of the cell voltages or another pack voltage reading, and sets the code when the difference stays too large.
s: MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Implausible state-of-charge or range display
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist
c: Drift or calibration error of measurement channel C
Cell voltage acquisition faulty, reference sum wrong
Battery controller software needs an update

P0B1B.d: P0B1B sets when pack voltage measurement C delivers a reading below its plausible lower limit. Typical electrical causes are a sense lead shorted to ground, an open fuse or resistor in the sense path, or a defective controller input.
s: Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system
MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist
c: Sense lead of channel C shorted to ground
Fuse or resistor in the sense path open
Measurement input of the battery controller defective

P0B1C.d: P0B1C reports that pack voltage measurement C reads above its plausible upper limit. Usually the measurement path is at fault, for example a sense lead shorted to a higher potential, a defective controller input or a software error in the evaluation, rather than a real overvoltage of the pack.
s: MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist
c: Sense lead of channel C shorted to a higher potential
Evaluation error in battery controller software
Measurement input of the battery controller defective

P0B1D.d: P0B1D stands for an unsteady pack voltage measurement C: the signal jumps, drops out for moments or changes faster than a real battery voltage can. Because the fault often clears itself, it is frequently found only as a stored code.
s: Warning comes and goes, often stored as history
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist
Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system
c: Loose or corroded sense connector or terminal
Chafed sense lead with intermittent contact

P0B1E.d: Voltage sense D is the fourth and last pack voltage measurement in the SAE J2012 scheme. P0B1E is its general circuit code: the battery controller treats this input as electrically faulty, for example open or without a usable raw signal.
s: MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist
Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system
c: Voltage sense lead D or its fuse open
Measurement input of the battery controller defective

P0B1F.d: P0B1F says pack voltage measurement D is electrically present but disagrees with what the controller expects, typically the sum of cell voltages or a parallel pack measurement. It is a plausibility fault, not an open or shorted circuit.
s: MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Implausible state-of-charge or range display
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist
c: Drift or calibration error of measurement channel D
Cell voltage acquisition faulty, reference sum wrong
Battery controller software needs an update

P0B20.d: P0B20 sets when pack voltage measurement D falls below its plausible minimum. The cause is usually electrical: a sense lead shorted to ground, an interrupted fuse or resistor in the measurement path, or a damaged controller input.
s: Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system
MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist
c: Sense lead of channel D shorted to ground
Fuse or resistor in the sense path open
Measurement input of the battery controller defective

P0B21.d: P0B21 means pack voltage measurement D reports more than its plausible maximum. As with the other high codes, the measurement path is the main suspect, for example a sense lead shorted to a higher potential, a faulty input stage or an evaluation error in software, not an actual overcharged pack.
s: MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist
c: Sense lead of channel D shorted to a higher potential
Evaluation error in battery controller software
Measurement input of the battery controller defective

P0B22.d: P0B22 completes the voltage sense D series and reports an intermittent or erratic pack voltage measurement D: the reading jumps, drops out briefly or changes implausibly fast, then recovers. Current code lists title it this way; the older label Generator Phase U Current Sensor Circuit does not belong to this number.
s: Warning comes and goes, often stored as history
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist
Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system
c: Loose or corroded sense connector or terminal
Chafed sense lead with intermittent contact

P0B23.d: P0B23 is the general fault for the voltage of hybrid/EV battery A, the first of up to four sub-batteries or energy stores (A to D) that the battery controller evaluates separately; which physical unit carries the letter is up to the manufacturer. The code says that the measured voltage of this unit no longer fits the expected value, without the finer split into unstable (P0B24), low (P0B25) or high (P0B26).
s: Hybrid/EV system or high-voltage battery warning on
MIL on
Battery power limited, less electric drive or assist
Charging or recuperation restricted
c: Weak or failing cells or module in battery A
Fault in the voltage sense leads or connectors of battery A
Battery controller software or internal measurement fault

P0B24.d: P0B24 reports that the voltage of hybrid/EV battery A is unstable: it swings or jumps more than the battery controller accepts instead of staying steadily too low or too high (P0B25, P0B26). Stellantis lists P0B24-00 with MIL on the Jeep Wrangler 4xe and Grand Cherokee 4xe, together with pack voltage variation, cell balancing and state-of-health codes; the cure is new software for the battery pack control module or,
s: MIL on
Hybrid/EV system or high-voltage battery warning on
Vehicle may not start (Jeep 4xe)
Warning comes and goes, fault often stored as intermittent
c: Battery controller software (Jeep 4xe BPCM/HCP, Ford BECM updates)
Loose busbar, terminal or sense contact in battery A
Cell with rising internal resistance in battery A

P0B25.d: P0B25 sets when the voltage of hybrid/EV battery A drops below the window the controller expects. Bentley uses it in two different systems.
s: Bentley Dynamic Ride fault warning, roll control inactive
MIL on
Hybrid/EV system or high-voltage battery warning on
Battery power limited, less electric drive or assist
c: Internal fault of the energy store, e.g. Bentley 48 V super capacitor
Aged or unbalanced cells pulling the unit voltage down
Voltage measurement fault in the controller or sense leads

P0B26.d: P0B26 means the voltage of hybrid/EV battery A is above the permitted value. Bentley documents it in the 48 V Dynamic Ride system of the Continental GT and Flying Spur, stored in address 0021 with symptom code 28672; the prescribed repair is replacing the super capacitor.
s: Bentley Dynamic Ride fault warning, roll control inactive
MIL on
Hybrid/EV system or high-voltage battery warning on
Charging or recuperation restricted
c: Failing energy store, e.g. Bentley 48 V super capacitor
Cell group charged too high, balancing not effective
Voltage measurement fault in the controller or sense leads

P0B27.d: P0B27 is the general voltage fault of hybrid/EV battery B, the second separately monitored sub-battery or energy store. It covers a voltage that does not match expectation without saying whether it is unstable (P0B28), too low (P0B29) or too high (P0B2A).
s: Hybrid/EV system or high-voltage battery warning on
MIL on
Battery power limited, less electric drive or assist
Charging or recuperation restricted
c: Weak or failing cells or module in battery B
Fault in the voltage sense leads or connectors of battery B
Battery controller software or internal measurement fault

P0B28.d: P0B28 flags an unstable voltage of hybrid/EV battery B: the reading fluctuates beyond what the battery controller tolerates. Stellantis documents it with P0B28-00 on the Jeep Wrangler 4xe: the MIL is on, and the bulletin warns that after 49 days with this MIL lit the vehicle is no longer allowed to start.
s: MIL on
Start inhibited after a long period with the MIL lit (Jeep 4xe: 49 days)
Hybrid/EV system or high-voltage battery warning on
Warning comes and goes, fault often stored as intermittent

Loose busbar, terminal or sense contact in battery B
Cell with rising internal resistance in battery B

P0B29.d: P0B29 sets when the voltage of hybrid/EV battery B stays below the range the controller expects for the present state of charge and load. It is the low counterpart to P0B2A; fluctuating readings belong to P0B28 and the general fault to P0B27.
s: Hybrid/EV system or high-voltage battery warning on
MIL on
Battery power limited, less electric drive or assist
Electric-only driving unavailable
c: Aged cells with lost capacity in battery B
Deep discharge or self-discharge after standstill
Voltage measurement fault in the controller or sense leads

P0B2A.d: P0B2A is stored when the voltage of hybrid/EV battery B rises above its permitted upper limit. It mirrors P0B29 (too low), while P0B28 covers fluctuation and P0B27 the general fault.

MIL on
Charging or recuperation restricted
Battery power limited, less electric drive or assist
c: Cell group in battery B charged too high, balancing ineffective
Voltage measurement fault in the controller or sense leads

P0B2B.d: P0B2B is the general voltage fault of hybrid/EV battery C, the third sub-battery or energy store that a controller can monitor on its own. It signals an implausible voltage of this unit without the detail given by P0B2C (unstable), P0B2D (low) or P0B2E (high).

MIL on
Battery power limited, less electric drive or assist
Charging or recuperation restricted
c: Weak or failing cells or module in battery C
Fault in the voltage sense leads or connectors of battery C
Battery controller software or internal measurement fault

P0B2C.d: P0B2C indicates that the voltage of hybrid/EV battery C is unstable, meaning it changes faster or further than plausible for the current load, while a steady deviation would set P0B2D or P0B2E. No manufacturer documents P0B2C publicly.

Charging or recuperation restricted
External charging refused

P0B33.d: The high-voltage service disconnect is the removable plug, usually fused, that splits the traction battery for safe servicing. A low-voltage detection loop runs through the plug, and the battery controller reads it to know whether the plug is seated; patents from Ford and Lear describe this loop, which opens before the main contacts part.
s: Vehicle does not enter ready mode or will not start
High-voltage system warning and MIL on
Charging not possible
c: Service disconnect plug not fully seated or locked after service
Chafed, open or shorted detection loop wiring between plug base and battery controller
Corroded or spread terminals in the plug or its base

P0B34.d: P0B34 covers a plausibility fault of the service disconnect detection: the signal is electrically within limits but does not match what the controller expects, for example a plug reported as removed while the high-voltage bus still shows voltage, or a state that changes without a matching event. Audi lists P0B3400 in the controller at address 008C of the 2025 Q5 e-hybrid, together with U029A00 and U059B00, and asks t
s: Electrical system or high-voltage warning
No ready mode or charging interrupted
Related network codes stored at the same time
c: Battery controller software fault (Audi case under investigation)
Loose plug or worn contacts giving an implausible detection state
Increased resistance in the detection loop
Communication fault between battery controller and other modules

P0B35.d: P0B35 sets when the service disconnect detection signal stays below its lower limit. Where the loop is coded with a resistor in the plug, as in a Lear patent, a reading near zero typically points to a short to ground in the loop wiring; the exact meaning depends on how the manufacturer powers the input.
s: No ready mode or stall with a stop-safely message
MIL and high-voltage warning on
Charging not possible
c: Detection loop wire chafed and shorted to ground
Moisture or corrosion in the plug base bridging to ground
Coding element in the plug shorted

P0B36.d: P0B36 sets when the service disconnect detection signal stays above its upper limit. With a pulled-up input this usually means a short to a voltage source or a missing coding element in the plug; on some designs an open loop also reads high, so manufacturers separate it with P0B37 only where they can tell the cases apart.
s: Vehicle not ready to drive
MIL and high-voltage warning on
Charging blocked
c: Detection loop wire shorted to a supply voltage
Open loop or missing contact read as high signal
Wrong or damaged service disconnect plug without proper coding

P0B37.d: P0B37 means the controller sees the service disconnect as open, either because the plug is really removed or because its detection loop is broken. Ford uses the code in the battery energy control module of the 2013-2016 C-Max Energi: bulletins SSM 46108 and TSB 17-0015 describe intermittent stalls or no crank with a Stop Safely Now message and MIL, stored with U3012 and, in another module, the interlock code P0A0A.
s: Intermittent stall or no crank
Stop Safely Now message and MIL
High-voltage interlock code stored in another module
c: Low-voltage interlock wiring chafed with intermittent short to ground (Ford C-Max)
Service disconnect plug removed, loose or not locked
Open terminal in the plug base or interlock connector

P0B38.d: Hybrid and electric drives cool the inverter and motor electronics with electric coolant pumps; J2012 numbers them A, B and C. P0B38 sets when the controller detects an open or general fault in the control line of pump B, typically by checking the driver output for missing load current.
s: Hybrid system or coolant warning, MIL on
Reduced electric drive power when electronics get hot
Pump not running audibly after switch-on
c: Pump connector loose, corroded or terminal pushed out
Open control wire between controller and pump
Pump electronics or motor failed open
Driver stage in the controlling module faulty

P0B39.d: P0B39 sets when the control signal of motor electronics coolant pump B is lower than the controller expects, usually a short to ground on the command line or a pump input that pulls the line down. On a low-side switched or PWM line the module sees the voltage stuck low while it commands the pump off.
s: MIL and hybrid or coolant warning
Pump runs permanently or not at all, depending on circuit design
Power limitation at high load or heat
c: Control wire shorted to ground, often chafed at brackets
Pump electronics pulling the control input low
Coolant or water in the pump connector
Driver stage in the controlling module faulty

P0B3A.d: P0B3A sets when the control signal of motor electronics coolant pump B stays higher than expected, typically a short to battery voltage on the command line or, with some driver designs, an open pump input that floats high. The module then cannot switch the pump as requested.
s: MIL and hybrid or coolant warning
Pump cannot be switched off or on as commanded
Reduced electric power when the inverter heats up
c: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Pump control input open so the line floats high
Controller software misjudging the circuit, fixed by update
Driver stage in the controlling module faulty

P0B3B.d: Voltage sense A to Z and beyond are the cell or cell-group sense channels of the battery monitoring electronics, unlike the pack voltage sense codes P0ABA and P0B14 ff, which measure the whole pack. P0B3B is the circuit code for channel A.
s: MIL or powertrain warning, Stop Safely Now message possible
No start or no charging
Fail-safe EV mode with limited speed and sudden loss of power
c: Open cell sense line, splice or bus bar connection inside the pack
Intermittent fault in the flexible printed circuit to the battery controller (Ford Mach-E)
Sensor software misreading inverter noise, fixed by update (Honda)
Internal failure of the traction battery requiring pack replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV)

P0B3C.d: P0B3C flags a cell voltage channel A that reads plausible values but does not follow the other cells. GM runs this check in Hybrid Powertrain Control Processor 2 as a stuck-in-range test: while the average cell voltage moves by at least 0.005 V in one direction between samples, channel A must move as well; 35 failures in 40 samples at 100 ms set the code, Type A, one trip.
s: MIL on, often with several voltage sense codes
Reduced electric range or no electric drive
Contactor related codes stored at the same time
c: Battery controller software, fixed by reprogramming (FCA Pacifica)
Cell voltage measurement channel frozen inside the monitoring electronics
High resistance in the cell sense line or its connection
Cell monitoring board failure inside the pack

P0B3D.d: P0B3D sets when cell voltage channel A reads below the lowest value a real cell can have, which points to the measurement rather than the cell. GM sets it in the battery energy control module when cell voltage A is 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s within a 2 s window, Type A, one trip, provided no open sense line, communication or balancing fault is active.
s: MIL on
Start-stop and electric assist unavailable
Hybrid battery power limited
c: Battery pack control module software, fixed by update (Ram eTorque)
Sense line shorted to the adjacent line or to the cell negative
Measurement input of the cell monitoring chip failed

P0B3E.d: P0B3E sets when cell voltage channel A reads above any value a healthy lithium-ion cell reaches, so the reading is treated as a sensing fault. GM sets it in the battery energy control module when cell voltage A is 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s within a 2 s window, Type A, one trip.
s: MIL on, possibly without noticeable drivability change
Electric drive or start-stop disabled
Charging limited
c: Battery pack control module software causing a false MIL (FCA)
Open sense line letting the input float high
Measurement input of the cell monitoring chip failed

P0B3F.d: P0B3F is reserved for a cell voltage channel A that jumps or drops out briefly instead of failing steadily. No manufacturer documents P0B3F publicly.
s: MIL or hybrid warning that comes and goes
Occasional loss of electric drive or assist
c: Loose or cracked cell tap connection
Fretting or vibration damage at the monitoring board connector
Electrical noise from inverter or motor coupling into the sense lines

P0B40.d: P0B40 is the circuit code of cell voltage sense channel B, the second cell or cell group the battery monitoring electronics measures; pack-level voltage uses P0ABA and P0B14 ff instead. GM applies the same open sense line test as on channel A: a 1.3 V jump between neighbouring cells, under 36 mV with balancing on, or splice voltage above 0.1 V (bus bar 0.5 V) for 0.6 s, Type A, one trip.
s: Wrench indicator or MIL, Stop Safely Now message possible
No start condition
Battery cannot be charged
c: Open cell sense line, splice or bus bar connection inside the pack
Intermittent flexible printed circuit cable in the battery controller (Ford Mach-E, e-Transit)
Internal traction battery failure requiring replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV)

P0B41.d: P0B41 reports that cell voltage channel B gives values inside the normal range that fail a plausibility check against the other cells. In GM's 2019 tables Hybrid Powertrain Control Processor 2 compares sample-to-sample changes: if the average cell voltage trends by at least 0.005 V while channel B stays unchanged, a failure is counted, and 35 of 40 samples at 100 ms set the code, Type A, one trip, with system voltage
s: MIL on, often with several voltage sense codes
Electric drive reduced or unavailable
Contactor related codes stored at the same time
c: Battery controller software, fixed by reprogramming (FCA Pacifica)
Cell voltage measurement channel frozen inside the monitoring electronics
High resistance in the cell sense line or its connection
Cell monitoring board failure inside the pack

P0B42.d: P0B42 sets when cell voltage channel B reads implausibly low, below what any usable cell would show. GM's battery energy control module sets it at 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s within a 2 s window, Type A, one trip, and only when no open sense line, slave communication or balancing fault is present.
s: MIL on
Start-stop inoperative
Vehicle behaves as if running on the engine only
c: Battery pack control module software causing a false MIL (FCA eTorque)
Sense line shorted to the adjacent line or to the cell negative
Measurement input of the cell monitoring chip failed

P0B43.d: P0B43 sets when cell voltage channel B reads higher than a lithium-ion cell can physically reach in service, so the controller blames the measurement path. GM documents the criteria for its battery energy control module: cell voltage B at 4.8 V or above for 1.4 s within a 2 s window, Type A, one trip, with open sense line, communication and balancing faults ruled out first.
s: MIL and hybrid warning on
Charging or electric drive limited
c: Open sense line letting the input float high
Battery controller software misreading the channel
Measurement input of the cell monitoring chip failed

P0B44.d: P0B44 is the J2012 slot for a cell voltage channel B whose reading jumps or drops out for short moments rather than failing permanently. No manufacturer documents P0B44 publicly.
s: MIL or hybrid warning that comes and goes
Occasional loss of electric drive or assist
c: Loose or cracked cell tap connection
Fretting or vibration damage at the monitoring board connector
Electrical noise from inverter or motor coupling into the sense lines

P0B45.d: Voltage sense C is the third cell or cell-group measuring channel of the battery monitoring electronics, not a pack voltage input like P0ABA. P0B45 reports an electrical break in that channel.
s: Vehicle does not start or does not become ready to drive
High-voltage battery no longer charges
Powertrain warning (wrench) and Stop Safely Now message
c: Open cell sense tap, splice or bus bar connection on channel C
Intermittent flexible printed circuit between cells and battery controller (Ford Mach-E, E-Transit)
Internal traction battery failure requiring pack replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV)

P0B46.d: With P0B46 the channel C wiring is intact; the value on it looks plausible but no longer behaves like a real cell. GM's 2019 tables run the test in Hybrid Powertrain Control Processor 2: whenever the average cell voltage trends by at least 0.005 V in one direction, channel C has to follow; if it stays frozen in 35 of 40 samples at 100 ms, the code sets, Type A.
s: MIL on without noticeable driving fault
Reduced electric power or hybrid assist
Contactor or precharge codes stored at the same time (Pacifica)
c: Battery controller software misjudging the channel, fixed by reflash (Chrysler Pacifica PHEV)
Measuring chip input for channel C stuck at a constant value
High-resistance cell tap damping the channel C signal

P0B47.d: P0B47 is stored when channel C delivers a voltage too low to come from a working cell or block, so the controller blames the measurement rather than the battery. GM documents two implementations.
s: Hybrid system warning and MIL
Electric drive or engine start-stop no longer available
Battery power limited, sluggish acceleration
c: Sense lines of channel C shorted to each other or to a neighbouring tap
Failed measuring input in the battery monitoring module
Loose or corroded block connector shared by blocks 3 and 4 (GM two-mode)

P0B48.d: No healthy lithium-ion cell reaches 4.8 V, which is why GM's battery energy control module treats a channel C reading of 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s within a 2 s window as a sensing fault and stores P0B48, Type A, one trip. On the 2012 two-mode full-size hybrids the threshold is scaled to a nickel-metal hydride block: block 3 above 23 V in 15 of 20 samples, Type B, two trips.
s: MIL and hybrid or EV system warning
Reduced charge and discharge power
Plug-in charging refused
c: Channel C sense line touching a tap of higher potential
Failed measuring input or reference in the monitoring electronics
Monitoring software fault, check for controller updates

P0B49.d: P0B49 is reserved for a channel C signal that jumps or drops out briefly instead of failing for good. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; GM, which uses the other four channel C codes, has no erratic test for it in its published tables.
s: Warning light that appears and disappears
Occasional short loss of electric drive power
c: Loose crimp or connector on the channel C sense line
Cracked solder joint on the cell monitoring board
Electrical noise from the inverter coupling into the sense line

P0B4A.d: P0B4A is the open-circuit code of cell sense channel D, the fourth measuring channel of the battery monitoring electronics. GM checks it in the battery energy control module with the same open sense line logic as the other channels: a gap of 1.3 V or more between adjacent cells, under 36 mV on a cell being balanced, or splice voltages above 0.1 V or 0.5 V at a bus bar, for 0.6 s, Type A.
s: No start or vehicle will not go into ready mode
Charging not possible
Several sense channel codes stored together
c: Open channel D sense tap or connector (code set alone)
Faulty BECM flexible printed circuit affecting several channels (Ford Mach-E, E-Transit)
Internal traction battery fault (Ford Fusion PHEV)

P0B4B.d: How the plausibility of channel D is judged depends on the pack. On the 2012 GM two-mode hybrids the battery pack control module multiplies block 4 by 20 and compares it with the pack voltage; a gap above 70 V in 160 of 170 samples sets P0B4B, Type B, two trips.
s: MIL, often after several drives
Limited hybrid assist or electric range
c: Outdated battery controller software (Chrysler Pacifica PHEV)
Block or cell voltage measurement drifting away from the pack voltage
Measuring input of channel D frozen at a constant value

P0B4C.d: From the driver's seat P0B4C looks like a battery problem: the hybrid warning comes on and electric power is cut back. Technically it is a measuring fault on cell channel D, whose reading has fallen below what even a deeply discharged cell would show.
s: Hybrid warning message and MIL
Electric power and regeneration cut back
Engine runs more often than usual
c: Short between channel D sense line and a neighbouring line
Defective input on the cell monitoring module
Corroded tap shared by blocks 4 and 5 (GM two-mode)

P0B4D.d: P0B4D sets when cell sense channel D reports more voltage than the cell or block behind it can deliver. GM's limits are 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s within 2 s on lithium-ion packs (battery energy control module, Type A, one trip) and above 23 V for block 4 of the 2012 two-mode hybrids (15 of 20 samples, Type B, two trips).
s: MIL and battery system warning
Reduced acceleration and regenerative braking
Charging power limited or charging refused
c: Channel D sense lead contacting a tap of higher potential
Damaged measuring input in the monitoring electronics
Moisture or contamination on the monitoring board creating leakage paths

P0B4E.d: P0B4E completes the five-code set of cell channel D. Where P0B4A means a lasting open circuit, P0B4B a frozen or implausible value and P0B4C or P0B4D a reading beyond fixed limits, this code is meant for short, irregular dropouts and spikes.
s: Intermittent hybrid warning, often on rough roads
Fault not reproducible during workshop test
c: Connector or tap losing contact under vibration
Solder joint or crimp cracked by thermal cycling

P0B4F.d: Cell sense channel E is the fifth measuring path between the battery cells and the monitoring electronics; P0B4F means the controller sees it as electrically open. Ford's experience shows how serious this can be: on 2019-2020 Fusion plug-in hybrids P0B4F appears among up to fourteen open-line codes from P0B3B to P0B7C with a no-start condition, and the bulletin prescribes replacing the high-voltage battery.
s: No start
Battery cannot be charged
Stop Safely Now message while driving
c: Internal failure of the high-voltage battery (Ford Fusion PHEV)
Intermittent BECM flexible printed circuit (Ford Mach-E, E-Transit)
Broken channel E sense lead, splice or bus bar contact

P0B50.d: On the 2020 Chrysler Pacifica plug-in hybrid P0B50 is called Voltage Sense 5 Circuit Performance and rarely comes alone: the FCA bulletin lists it with the other sense channels, contactor stuck codes, a long precharge time and wake-up circuit faults, all cured by updating the battery pack control module. Some owners also notice that scheduled charging fails because the pack does not wake up.
s: MIL on
Scheduled charging does not start
Premature oil change or fuel refresh message (Pacifica)
c: Battery pack control module software, fixed by reflash (Chrysler Pacifica PHEV)
Channel E reading frozen in the measuring chip
Block voltage measurement drifting from pack voltage (GM two-mode)

P0B51.d: P0B51 tells that cell sense channel E reads near zero. GM's battery energy control module only runs this check under clear conditions: the module is in run, crank or accessory mode, the second protection self-test is not running, and no slave communication, open sense line, balancing or internal performance fault is active.
s: MIL and hybrid system warning
Electric-only driving unavailable
c: Channel E sense line shorted to its neighbour
Faulty input on the cell monitoring slave board
Pin backed out of the monitoring harness connector

P0B52.d: The threshold behind P0B52 is chosen so that only a measurement error can reach it. A lithium-ion cell is fully charged at roughly 4.2 V, yet GM's battery energy control module waits for 4.8 V or more on channel E, for 1.4 s within 2 s, before storing the code as Type A, one trip.
s: Charging stops early or is refused
MIL and reduced battery power
Shorter electric range
c: Channel E sense line contacting a higher cell tap
Faulty measuring input or reference in the monitoring module

P0B53.d: P0B53 belongs to cell sense channel E and describes a signal that is sometimes fine and sometimes not. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Warning that clears and returns
Brief loss of electric power while driving
c: Intermittent contact at the channel E tap or connector
Chafed sense lead touching briefly under movement
Marginal component on the monitoring board

P0B54.d: Ford's 2024 special service message for the 2023 Mustang Mach-E and E-Transit is the most instructive case for P0B54: vehicles built up to 9 December 2023 could store this and the other open-line codes from P0B3B to P0B5E, show the wrench light, refuse to start or charge, or display Stop Safely Now, and the cause was an intermittent BECM flexible printed circuit cable rather than the cells. The 2019-2020 Fusion PHEV
s: Powertrain malfunction (wrench) indicator on
No start or no charging
Stop Safely Now message
c: Intermittent BECM flexible printed circuit cable (Ford Mach-E, E-Transit built to Dec 2023)
Open channel F tap or splice
Internal traction battery failure (Ford Fusion PHEV)

P0B55.d: P0B55 is the plausibility code of cell channel F: the signal exists and lies inside its range, yet it does not move like the rest of the pack. On the 2016 Chevrolet Volt the vehicle integration control module checks whether channel F moves in the same direction as the average cell voltage, failing it after 7 seconds in an 8 second window, Type A; GM's 2019 tables use 35 failures in 40 samples of 100 ms.
s: MIL with otherwise normal driving
Reduced hybrid or electric performance
c: Battery controller software, fixed by update (Chrysler Pacifica PHEV)
Channel F measuring input stuck or slow to respond
Increased resistance in the channel F tap or connector

P0B56.d: The GM two-mode hybrids of 2012, Tahoe, Yukon, Escalade, Silverado and Sierra, show a detail of P0B56 that lithium-ion packs lack. Their nickel-metal hydride pack is read in blocks, channel F being block 6, and the battery pack control module sets the code only when block 6 and block 7 both read under 2 V in 15 of 20 samples at 100 ms, Type B, two trips; a shared sense wire between the blocks is the obvious suspect t
s: Hybrid system warning, MIL after the second drive (two-mode)
Engine runs continuously, no electric launch
Lower fuel economy
c: Fault in the sense wire shared by blocks 6 and 7 (GM two-mode)
Channel F sense line shorted to a neighbouring line
Failed input on the cell monitoring electronics

P0B57.d: P0B57 stands for an implausibly high value on cell sense channel F, as opposed to P0B56 for an implausibly low one and P0B55 for a frozen value. GM uses fixed upper limits: 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s within 2 s in the battery energy control module of its lithium-ion systems (Type A, one trip), and above 23 V for block 6 in the 2012 two-mode trucks (15 of 20 samples, Type B, two trips).
s: MIL and battery warning
Battery charging limited
Weaker acceleration in hybrid mode
c: Channel F sense lead touching a higher potential
Measuring input or reference fault in the module

P0B58.d: P0B58 is reserved for an erratic signal on cell sense channel F, and the honest state is short: no manufacturer documents this code publicly. The neighbouring codes are well covered; Ford and GM use the open circuit code P0B54, GM and Chrysler the range code P0B55, GM the fixed low and high limits.
s: Sporadic warning depending on road or temperature
Occasional brief power reduction
c: Sense tap of channel F loosening under vibration
Damaged section of the flexible sense circuit

P0B59.d: Voltage sense G is the seventh cell measuring channel; how many cells or groups it covers depends on how the manufacturer splits the pack among monitoring chips. P0B59 is its open-circuit code.
s: Vehicle not ready to drive
Charging blocked
Wrench light or hybrid warning
c: Open channel G tap, splice or bus bar contact
Intermittent BECM flexible circuit (Ford Mach-E, E-Transit)
Internal traction battery failure (Ford Fusion PHEV)

P0B5A.d: P0B5A asks whether cell channel G behaves like a real cell. GM answers that question in three ways across its programmes.
s: MIL without obvious drivability change
Limited hybrid assist
c: Channel G measuring input frozen or drifting
Block 7 reading out of line with pack voltage (GM two-mode)
Monitoring software issue, check for updates

P0B5B.d: When P0B5B appears, the battery controller has seen cell sense channel G at a level no usable cell would show, and it shuts down or restricts electric operation to stay on the safe side. GM documents the trigger for its lithium-ion systems as cell voltage G at or below 0.2 V for 1.4 s in a 2 s window, Type A, with the test held off while communication, open line or balancing faults are active.
s: Hybrid system warning and MIL
Electric drive disabled or restricted
c: Channel G sense line shorted to a neighbouring line
Damaged or backed-out pin in the monitoring connector
Failed measuring input on the monitoring module

P0B5C.d: P0B5C marks an out-of-range high reading on cell sense channel G. For a technician the quickest plausibility check is arithmetic: the sum of all cell or block readings should match the pack voltage, so a single channel that reads far too high while the total stays normal is a sensing fault.
s: MIL and hybrid or EV warning
Charging limited or refused
c: Channel G sense lead touching a higher cell tap
Faulty measuring input or reference in the module
Contamination or moisture on the monitoring board

P0B5D.d: P0B5D is the J2012 code for an unsteady signal on cell sense channel G, a reading that flickers or drops out for moments without staying beyond a limit. No manufacturer documents P0B5D publicly.
s: Warning that disappears after restart and returns
Brief reduction of electric power
c: Marginal contact at the channel G tap or connector
Sense harness under strain, losing contact with pack movement

P0B5E.d: P0B5E flags a broken measuring path on voltage sense H, the eighth cell tap channel read by the battery monitoring electronics. In GM's 2019 tables the battery energy control module runs an open sense line test within a 0.6 s window: neighbouring cells diverging by 1.3 V or more, a cell under 36 mV while its balancing switch is on, or a splice above 0.1 V (0.5 V at a bus bar splice) sets it as Type A.
s: Powertrain malfunction (wrench) indicator and Stop Safely Now message
Vehicle does not start or does not become ready to drive
High-voltage battery cannot be charged
c: Intermittent flexible printed circuit cable at the battery controller (Ford Mach-E, E-Transit 2023)
Open cell tap, splice or bus bar connection on channel H
Internal traction battery failure requiring pack replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV)

P0B5F.d: With P0B5F the channel H wiring is intact, but the value it delivers does not fit the rest of the battery. GM runs two quite different plausibility tests.
s: Hybrid system warning with MIL
Reduced electric assist or regeneration
Inaccurate state-of-charge display
c: Block or cell voltage input for channel H drifting away from the true value
Measuring chip input stuck at a constant value
Faulty pack voltage reference distorting the comparison

P0B60.d: P0B60 means channel H reports less voltage than any healthy cell or block could hold, so the measurement itself is suspect. GM publishes three variants.
s: MIL and hybrid or EV system warning
Electric drive power limited or switched off
Charging interrupted
c: Channel H sense lead shorted to ground or to the next lower tap
Failed measuring input on the cell monitoring board
Cell or block on channel H actually collapsed

P0B61.d: A lithium-ion cell cannot sit much above about 4.2 V, so when channel H reads 4.8 V or more the GM battery energy control module concludes the sense circuit is wrong and stores P0B61 after 1.4 s within a 2 s window, Type A. GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid sets the same code at more than 4.65 V on the cell sense line in 7 of 10 samples, Type B, while the 2012 two-mode hybrids treat H as nickel-metal hydride block 8 and only
s: Charging refused or stopped early
MIL with reduced electric power
c: Channel H sense lead in contact with a higher cell tap
Lost reference connection letting the measuring input float
Internal fault of the cell monitoring chip

P0B62.d: P0B62 describes a channel H signal that jumps or cuts out for moments rather than failing permanently. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Warning appears occasionally and clears after a restart
Short interruptions of electric drive
c: Intermittent contact at the channel H connector or flexible circuit
Cracked solder joint on the monitoring board
Inverter noise coupling into the sense line

P0B63.d: Channel I is the ninth sense input of the battery monitoring chain, and P0B63 reports that its circuit is open. GM shows how differently this can be detected.
s: Vehicle will not start or enter ready mode
Service hybrid or EV system warning
Electric mode unavailable
c: Broken channel I sense wire, crimp or cell tap
Internal traction battery fault, pack replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV)
Corroded or loose connector at the cell monitoring board

P0B64.d: P0B64 is a rationality fault: channel I is connected and reads a believable number, yet it does not move with the other cells. GM's 2016 Chevrolet Volt compares the movement of each cell with the average; if channel I does not follow when the average moves by more than 0.022 V, 7 out of 8 seconds fail the check, Type A.
s: MIL on, vehicle drives normally
Reduced hybrid assist or electric range
c: Channel I measuring input frozen at a constant value
Battery controller software misjudging the channel
High-resistance cell tap damping the signal

P0B65.d: The 2012 GM two-mode hybrids show a detail worth knowing for P0B65: their battery pack control module only declares channel I, nickel-metal hydride block 9, too low when block 9 and its neighbour block 10 both read under 2 V, and only after 15 of 20 samples at 100 ms; the fault is Type B and needs two trips. A single weak block alone therefore does not set it.
s: Hybrid system warning and MIL
Engine runs more often, electric assist reduced
Limited power in limp mode
c: Channel I sense lead shorted to ground or a lower tap
Connector fault affecting adjacent blocks 9 and 10 (two-mode)
Failed measuring input in the battery controller

P0B66.d: When channel I claims a voltage above what its cell or block can physically reach, the controller stores P0B66. The thresholds GM publishes depend on chemistry and architecture: lithium-ion packs with a battery energy control module set it at 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s in a 2 s window, Type A, one trip; the BAS Plus mild hybrid at above 4.65 V in 7 of 10 samples, Type B; the 2012 two-mode trucks, which measure nickel-me
s: Charging stops or is refused
MIL and reduced power
c: Channel I lead touching a higher-potential tap
Open reference or ground of the measuring chip
Genuinely overcharged cell after a charging control fault

P0B67.d: SAE J2012 reserves P0B67 for an unsteady signal on channel I, meaning readings that spike, drop and recover. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and none of the GM tables that define the other four channel I codes includes an erratic test.
s: Sporadic warning without a reproducible pattern
Momentary drop in electric power
c: Sense contact on channel I opening under vibration or heat
Corroded terminal in the module connector

P0B68.d: For owners of a 2019 or 2020 Ford Fusion plug-in hybrid, P0B68 is best known from bulletin 23-2039: the car will not start, the battery energy control module stores one or more open sense line codes from P0B3B to P0B7C, and the prescribed repair is a complete high-voltage traction battery. Technically the code says that the tenth measuring channel, J, has lost its connection to the cells.
s: No start, vehicle does not become ready
Hybrid system warning on the cluster
Plug-in charging unavailable
c: Internal traction battery failure, pack replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV 2019-2020)
Open sense wire or cell tap on channel J
Bad bus bar or splice connection near channel J

P0B69.d: P0B69 is set when channel J is electrically present but its readings do not behave plausibly. GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid explains the logic most clearly: once the average cell voltage moves by more than 0.045 V, the cell under test must move in the same direction and by at least half as much; 20 failures in 40 samples set the code as Type B, two trips.
s: MIL without obvious driveability problem
Hybrid assist reduced
c: Channel J input reacting too little to real voltage changes
Calibration error in the battery controller

P0B6A.d: A reading of almost zero on channel J points to the measurement, not to the cell, and that is what P0B6A records. In GM's lithium-ion systems (2016 and 2019 tables) the battery energy control module sets it at 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s within 2 s, Type A.
s: Electric drive limited or unavailable
MIL and battery warning message
c: Channel J lead chafed through and shorted to ground
Damaged measuring input on the monitoring board
Cell on channel J internally shorted

P0B6B.d: On GM's 2012 two-mode hybrid trucks the battery is divided into 20 nickel-metal hydride blocks, and channel J is block 10. The battery pack control module samples it every 100 ms while the 12 V supply is between 9 and 18 V; if block 10 reports more than 23 V in 15 of 20 samples, P0B6B is stored as Type B, so the MIL comes on after the second trip.
s: MIL after the second drive (Type B systems)
Charging or regeneration restricted
Reduced electric power
c: Channel J lead shorted to a higher block or cell tap
Faulty measuring input in the battery pack control module

P0B6C.d: No manufacturer documents P0B6C publicly. The code stands for a channel J signal that is unstable, with brief jumps or dropouts, as opposed to the steady faults covered by P0B68 to P0B6B.
s: Intermittent warning light
Brief power reductions while driving
c: Marginal contact in the channel J harness or connector
Cracked solder joint on the monitoring electronics

P0B6D.d: P0B6D marks an open circuit on voltage sense K, the eleventh cell measuring channel. GM has used the code since its first published hybrid tables: in 2011 the open-line test already checked bus bar voltages, flagging more than 0.7 V.
s: Vehicle not ready to drive
Hybrid or EV system warning with MIL
Charging not possible
c: Loose or corroded bus bar connection at the channel K tap
Internal traction battery fault, pack replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV)
Broken sense wire between cells and monitoring board

P0B6E.d: In a nickel-metal hydride pack with 20 equal blocks, twenty times one block voltage should roughly equal the whole pack voltage. GM's 2012 two-mode hybrids use exactly this for P0B6E, assigned to block 11: the battery pack control module checks blocks 11 and 12, and if both scaled values deviate from the pack voltage sensor by more than 70 V in 160 of 170 samples, the code is set, Type B.
s: MIL after two trips
Less electric assist, more engine running
c: Block or cell voltage measurement of channel K out of calibration
Pack voltage sensor reading off, distorting the comparison
Measuring input stuck at one value

P0B6F.d: GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid, the eAssist system in table 13OBDG05C, gives P0B6F a simple rule: if the cell sense line for channel K measures below 1.4 V in 7 of 10 samples at 200 ms while the 12 V supply is above 8.8 V, the code is stored as Type B, two trips. Since a lithium-ion cell in use never falls that low, the value must come from a short or a failed input.
s: Hybrid warning and MIL after the second trip
Auto stop and electric assist disabled
c: Channel K sense line shorted to ground or a lower tap
Failed measuring input in the battery interface module
Blown protective element in the sense line

P0B70.d: P0B70 says that cell voltage K reads too high to be genuine. GM's 2019 battery energy control module sets it at 4.8 V or more, held for 1.4 s within 2 s, as a Type A fault with immediate MIL, and only when no communication loss, open sense line or internal module fault takes precedence.
s: Charging blocked
MIL and power limitation
c: Channel K lead in contact with a higher tap
Floating measuring input after loss of its lower reference

P0B71.d: P0B71 belongs to the unsteady fault type: the channel K reading flickers or drops out momentarily without staying beyond a fixed limit. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Warning that comes and goes
Occasional short loss of electric power
c: Fretting corrosion on channel K connector terminals
Sense harness under strain losing contact with movement

P0B72.d: P0B72 reports an open circuit on voltage sense L, the twelfth channel. One detail sets it apart from its neighbours: GM's 2011 hybrid tables list every open sense line code from P0B3B upward except P0B72 (and P0B90), so the early system did not use it, while L's range, low and high codes were present.
s: No start or no ready mode
Battery or hybrid system warning
Charging aborted
c: Open sense lead, crimp or cell tap on channel L
Internal traction battery failure, pack replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV)
High-resistance splice or bus bar joint

P0B73.d: Channel L delivers a value, but P0B73 tells you that the value is not credible. GM checks this in three ways.
s: MIL with normal driving behaviour
Reduced electric range or assist
c: Channel L input not following real cell voltage changes
Battery controller software or calibration issue
Corroded cell tap slowing the signal

P0B74.d: P0B74 is set when channel L reads implausibly low. On the 2012 GM two-mode hybrids, where L is nickel-metal hydride block 12 of 20, the battery pack control module needs both block 12 and block 13 under 2 V in 15 of 20 samples before it stores the code as Type B; no battery control module fault P0A1F may be active.
s: MIL and hybrid system warning
Electric operation restricted
Engine runs continuously on hybrids
c: Channel L sense lead shorted to a lower potential
Defective measuring input in the battery controller
Cell or block on channel L actually failed

P0B75.d: With P0B75 the battery controller rejects channel L because it reads above any value a real cell or block can reach. GM's lithium-ion systems in the 2016 Volt and the 2019 tables set it at 4.8 V or more over 1.4 s in a 2 s window, Type A, one trip; GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid at above 4.65 V in 7 of 10 samples, Type B.
s: Charging and regeneration limited
MIL and hybrid or EV warning
c: Channel L lead touching a higher tap
Floating measuring input after an open reference line
Real overvoltage of the cell after a charging fault

P0B76.d: P0B76 closes the channel L group and covers an erratic signal: values that jump or vanish briefly while the circuit otherwise works. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; GM, the only maker with public tables for L, defines open, plausibility, low and high tests for this channel but no erratic test, and the Ford bulletins name only the open-circuit code P0B72.
s: Warning clears after restart and comes back
Momentary power reduction
c: Intermittent contact at the channel L cell tap
Cracked solder joint on the monitoring board

P0B77.d: P0B77 flags an open or high-resistance tap on voltage sense M, the thirteenth cell channel. GM's 2019 battery energy control module checks seven cases: adjacent cells differing by 1.3 V or more, a balancing gate reading below 36 mV, or splice voltages above 0.1 V (0.5 V at a busbar splice).
s: MIL with hybrid or EV system warning
Vehicle may not start or go into ready mode
Charging blocked or limited
c: Open or corroded tap of sense lead M at the cell connector
Fault inside the traction battery (Ford Fusion PHEV TSB 23-2039)
High resistance at a splice or busbar joint in the sense path

P0B78.d: With P0B78 the controller doubts the reading of channel M rather than its wiring. GM's 2019 hybrid powertrain processor watches for a frozen value: whenever the average of all cells moves by more than 0.022 V, cell M must follow by at least 0.005 V in the same direction, and 35 failures in 40 samples at 100 ms set a Type A fault.
s: MIL on, often without noticeable driving change
Reduced electric assist or regeneration
c: Measuring channel M stuck at a fixed value
Battery controller software needing an update
Block 13 voltage drifting from the pack on two-mode NiMH packs

P0B79.d: P0B79 means that the voltage reported for sense M is too low to be real. GM's lithium-ion battery controllers of 2016 and 2019 set it at 0.2 V or less, held for 1.4 s inside a 2 s window, Type A, and only while no open sense line fault is active, so a broken lead is reported by P0B77 first.
s: MIL and service hybrid or EV system message
Electric drive or assist disabled
Engine runs continuously on hybrids
c: Sense lead M shorted to ground or a lower cell potential
Failed measuring input on the monitoring board
Cell or NiMH block on channel M actually collapsed

P0B7A.d: A reading on channel M above what any healthy cell can deliver produces P0B7A. For lithium-ion packs GM sets the line at 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s in a 2 s window and treats it as Type A, illuminating the MIL on the first trip.
s: MIL on from the first trip (GM lithium-ion, Type A)
Charging stopped or limited
Reduced electric power
c: Sense lead M in contact with a higher cell potential
Measuring input of channel M reading high
Real overvoltage of the cell after a balancing fault

P0B7B.d: P0B7B is reserved for a sense M signal that flickers: short dropouts or jumps while the circuit is otherwise intact. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Hybrid warning appearing and clearing again
Brief drops in electric power
c: Loose crimp or connector at the channel M tap
Chafed wire in the cell sense harness
Cracked solder joint on the monitoring board

P0B7C.d: Voltage sense N, the fourteenth channel, reports a broken or high-resistance sense lead with P0B7C. It is the last code in Ford's TSB 23-2039: 2019-2020 Fusion plug-in hybrids that fail to start with any open-circuit code from P0B3B up to P0B7C get a replacement traction battery; the bulletin names no channel beyond N.
s: No start or vehicle does not become ready
MIL and stop-safely or service message
Plug-in charging unavailable
c: Internal traction battery fault (Ford Fusion PHEV 2019-2020)
Sense lead N broken or with excessive resistance
Fault on the cell monitoring board

P0B7D.d: P0B7D concerns a channel N value that stays inside its limits yet does not behave like a real cell. GM's 2016 tables show how the same check is tuned per vehicle: the Chevrolet Volt fails when cell N does not move with the average for 7 of 8 seconds, while the Cadillac ELR counts 20 of 40 samples at 200 ms once the average shifts by more than 0.006 V; both are Type A.
s: MIL with hybrid service message
Shorter electric range or less assist
c: Channel N value not tracking the other cells
Block 14 or 15 voltage mismatch on two-mode NiMH packs

P0B7E.d: P0B7E sets when channel N reads below the lower plausibility limit. GM's 2016 program with a separate battery sense module uses less than 0.20 V and needs 14 failures in 18 samples, about 1.8 s at 100 ms each, before a Type A fault; the open-circuit test must not be failing at the same time.
s: MIL from the first trip on lithium-ion GM systems
Hybrid system limits power
Combustion engine does not shut off at standstill
c: Sense lead N shorted to a lower potential
Damaged input stage in the sense module
Deeply discharged or failed cell on channel N

P0B7F.d: Channel N reporting more voltage than a cell can hold leads to P0B7F. GM uses three thresholds depending on the system: 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s in 2 s on most lithium-ion battery controllers, above 4.90 V in 14 of 18 samples on the 2016 program with a separate sense module, both Type A, and above 4.65 V in 7 of 10 samples on the BAS Plus mild hybrid, Type B.
s: MIL and warning in the instrument cluster
Regenerative braking and charging limited
c: Sense lead N touching a higher potential
Drifted measuring input in the battery controller
Real overvoltage of the cell on channel N

P0B80.d: P0B80 describes an unsteady channel N signal: the voltage drops out or jumps for moments, then looks normal again. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Intermittent hybrid warning
Fault not present after restart
Occasional loss of electric power
c: Contact at the N tap opening under vibration
Fretting corrosion in the sense harness connector
Solder joint cracking with temperature cycles

P0B81.d: P0B81 stands for an open sense lead on channel O, the fifteenth cell tap. GM has used it from the start: the 2011 Volt battery tables already list P0B81 among the open sense line codes and detect, among other cases, a busbar connection voltage above 0.7 V.
s: MIL and propulsion system warning
Reduced power or no electric drive
c: Loose or high-resistance busbar joint at the O tap
Broken sense wire O in the battery harness

P0B82.d: P0B82 is a plausibility verdict on channel O. GM's 2016 program with a battery sense module asks cell O to trend at least 0.002 V in the direction of the average whenever the average moves by more than 0.022 V; 35 failed evaluations out of 40 set a Type A code.
s: MIL with otherwise normal driving
State of charge display jumps or is inaccurate
c: Channel O reading frozen in the monitoring electronics
Rising resistance in the O sense tap distorting the reading

P0B83.d: P0B83 reports that channel O reads implausibly low. It is not the same as an open lead: GM's lithium-ion controllers run this check only while no open sense line fault is present, so a broken wire shows as P0B81 instead.
s: MIL and hybrid warning lamp
Electric operation switched off
c: Short in the O sense path towards ground or a lower cell

P0B84.d: P0B84 is stored when channel O sits above the upper limit of a credible cell voltage. For GM lithium-ion packs that limit is 4.8 V, held 1.4 s in a 2 s window, Type A; the 2016 program with a separate sense module tolerates up to 4.90 V and counts 14 failures in 18 samples, also Type A.
s: MIL and battery warning
Charging ends early
Less electric assist
c: Sense lead O shorted to a higher cell tap
Monitoring input of channel O reading too high

P0B85.d: P0B85 would mark a channel O signal that is present but unsteady, with spikes or brief gaps. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; even GM, whose public tables cover channel O in detail from 2011 onward, defines only the open, rationality, low and high tests for it.
s: Warning that comes and goes
Short-term power reduction during driving
c: Loose busbar screw changing contact resistance at tap O
Moisture or corrosion in the sense harness connector
Cracked joint on the monitoring board

P0B86.d: P0B86 belongs to channel P, the sixteenth sense lead, and indicates that this lead has lost its connection to the cell. Comparing GM's tables shows how the timing evolved: the 2016 Volt battery controller decides within 0.6 s, the 2019 version waits 0.8 s in a 1.6 s window; both use the 1.3 V adjacent-cell, 36 mV balancing gate and splice criteria and are Type A.
s: MIL and hybrid system fault message
Vehicle runs only on the engine or with reduced power
c: Sense lead P open at the cell tap or connector
Excessive resistance in the sense line (corrosion, loose screw)
Defective input of the sense module

P0B87.d: P0B87 says channel P is delivering numbers that do not fit the rest of the battery. On GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid the cell under test must move at least 50 percent as far as the average cell voltage; if not, 20 failures in 40 samples set the code as Type B, i.e.
s: MIL after two trips on Type B systems
Engine start-stop or electric assist less frequent
c: Measuring electronics for channel P out of tolerance
Software or calibration of the battery controller
NiMH block 16 or 17 out of balance with the pack

P0B88.d: A too-low value on sense P, the sixteenth channel, is what P0B88 records. GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid sets it at a cell sense line below 1.4 V for 7 of 10 samples, sampled every 200 ms and only with the 12 V battery above 8.8 V; it rates the fault Type B.
s: MIL and reduced propulsion power
Auto stop no longer active
c: Lead P shorted to a lower potential or chassis
Defective input in the battery interface module

P0B89.d: P0B89 covers the opposite case to P0B88: the voltage reported on channel P is above the plausible range. GM's 2012 two-mode hybrids assign P to NiMH block 16 and set the code when the block exceeds 23 V in 15 of 20 samples at 100 ms, Type B, provided no battery controller fault P0A1F is active.
s: Charging restricted
MIL and hybrid warning
c: Lead P in contact with a higher cell tap
Input fault in the cell monitoring electronics
Genuine overvoltage of the cell or block

P0B8A.d: P0B8A is the erratic-signal member of the channel P group. There is no public manufacturer documentation for it: GM describes open, rationality, low and high diagnostics for sense P in its 2016 and 2019 tables, but none for an intermittent signal, and the Ford bulletins stop at channel N.
s: Warning lamp that goes out again
Occasional engine start without demand on hybrids
c: Fatigued wire at a bend of the sense harness
Connector losing contact as the pack warms up
Sporadic fault in the cell monitoring chip

P0B8B.d: P0B8B marks an open circuit on voltage sense Q, the seventeenth channel. In GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid tables Q is the first channel whose open test is blocked by code P1B37 instead of P1B36, which suggests it sits in the next measuring group of the battery interface module; the criterion stays lines N and N-1 below 1.4 V with a change above 0.5 V in 200 ms, 7 of 10 samples, Type B.
s: MIL and service vehicle message
Electric operation blocked or limited
Fuel consumption rises on hybrids
c: Sense lead Q open between cell tap and module
Loose or corroded connector at the second measuring group
Fault in the battery interface module

P0B8C.d: P0B8C is set when channel Q reports a voltage that fails the plausibility test against the other cells or the pack. On GM's 2012 two-mode trucks Q is NiMH block 17; the battery pack control module takes block 17 and block 18, multiplies each by twenty and compares with the measured pack voltage, failing beyond 70 V in 160 of 170 samples, Type B.
s: MIL with little change in driving
Usable battery capacity reduced
c: Block 17 or 18 voltage deviating on two-mode NiMH packs

P0B8D.d: P0B8D reports a voltage on sense Q below the lowest credible cell value. GM's lithium-ion battery controllers in the 2016 and 2019 tables use 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s within 2 s, Type A, and the 2016 program with a separate sense module 0.20 V with 14 of 18 samples.
s: MIL and reduced power mode
Engine runs more often on hybrids
c: Short in the Q sense path to a lower potential

P0B8E.d: Channel Q reporting an implausibly high voltage sets P0B8E. On the 2012 GM two-mode hybrids, where Q is NiMH block 17, the limit is 23 V for 15 of 20 samples, Type B, checked only while the 12 V system lies between 9 and 18 V.
s: Regeneration and charging limited
MIL and battery system warning
c: Damaged harness letting lead Q touch the next tap
Measuring input of channel Q reading high
Real cell overvoltage after a balancing failure

P0B8F.d: P0B8F closes the channel Q group and stands for a sense Q signal that is erratic rather than absent or out of range. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Sporadic hybrid or EV warning
Power briefly reduced, normal after restart
c: Cracked crimp at the channel Q tap
Damaged flexible circuit between cells and monitoring board
Cold solder joint at the measuring chip

P0B90.d: P0B90 is stored when the battery controller concludes that the tap of sense R, the eighteenth cell channel, is open or too resistive. GM's 2019 battery energy control module runs seven cases for it: neighbouring cells 1.3 V or more apart, a reading under 36 mV while the balancing gate is on, or splice voltages above 0.1 V (0.5 V at a busbar splice).
s: MIL with service hybrid or EV system warning
Reduced propulsion power or no ready mode
Charging interrupted or refused
c: Loose, corroded or broken tap of sense lead R
Excessive resistance at a splice or busbar joint feeding channel R
Faulty measuring or balancing input on the cell monitoring board

P0B91.d: Here the wiring of sense R is intact, but its value does not behave like a real cell. GM's 2019 hybrid powertrain processor demands that cell R moves at least 0.005 V in the same direction whenever the cell average shifts by more than 0.022 V; 35 failures out of 40 samples at 100 ms give a Type A fault.
s: MIL on, vehicle often drives normally
Less electric assist or regenerative braking
c: Measuring channel R reporting a stuck value
Outdated battery controller or hybrid processor software
Block 18 or 19 voltage drifting on two-mode NiMH packs

P0B92.d: P0B92 stands for an implausibly low reading on sense R. In GM's lithium-ion battery controllers of 2016 and 2019 the limit is 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s inside a 2 s window, Type A; the test is suspended while an open sense line fault is active, so a broken lead appears as P0B90 rather than P0B92.
s: MIL and hybrid or EV system message
Propulsion limited, possibly no restart
c: Sense lead R chafed through and touching ground or a lower cell
Failed input for channel R on the cell monitoring board
Cell or block on channel R genuinely collapsed

P0B93.d: A reading on sense R above anything a healthy cell could produce sets P0B93. GM's lithium-ion battery controllers of 2016 and 2019 use 4.8 V or more, held 1.4 s within 2 s, as a Type A fault.
s: MIL and hybrid system warning
Charging or regeneration cut back
Reduced power mode
c: Sense lead R in contact with a higher cell potential
Damaged measuring input for channel R
Cell on channel R actually overcharged
