P0B94.d: No manufacturer documents P0B94 publicly. The code is reserved for a sense R signal that drops out or jumps for short moments instead of failing steadily.
s: Warning appears and disappears between trips
Short power reductions, normal after restart
c: Crimp or terminal of lead R opening under vibration
Hairline crack in the flexible circuit carrying channel R
Moisture or contamination in the monitoring board connector

P0B95.d: P0B95 reports that the sense S lead, channel nineteen, no longer connects its cell reliably to the monitoring electronics. GM programmes with a separate battery sensor module (16OBDG02) measure this directly: after each normal reading the balancing gates switch in a test pattern, current flows through the sense wires and the voltage drop is turned into a line resistance.
s: MIL and hybrid or EV warning
Vehicle may refuse ready mode
Cell balancing no longer effective
c: High resistance in sense lead S from corrosion or a loose terminal
Sense lead S broken at the cell connector
Defective input of the battery sensor module for channel S

P0B96.d: P0B96 is a plausibility code: the voltage of sense S looks electrically valid but fails to track the rest of the pack. GM's eAssist mild hybrid requires cell S to move at least half as much as the other cells once the average changes by more than 0.045 V, judged over 20 of 40 samples at 200 ms, Type B.
s: MIL with little or no change in driving
Electric assist reduced at times
c: Measuring channel S frozen or lagging behind the other cells
Battery controller calibration requiring a software update
Block 19 or 20 out of step with the pack on two-mode NiMH batteries

P0B97.d: With P0B97 the controller sees sense S pulled close to zero. In the 2012 two-mode trucks, where S is the nickel-metal hydride block 19, the battery pack control module only sets it when block 19 and block 20 are both below 2 V in 15 of 20 samples, Type B, with the 12 V system between 9 and 18 V.
s: MIL and hybrid or EV warning message
Restricted power, engine may run more often on hybrids
c: Sense lead S shorted to ground or to the next lower cell
Defective channel S input on the monitoring board
Cell or NiMH block on channel S actually discharged

P0B98.d: P0B98 marks a sense S value that is too high to be a cell voltage. The thresholds vary with the battery chemistry and controller: GM's 2016 Volt and 2019 battery controllers flag 4.8 V or more after 1.4 s in 2 s (Type A), the 16OBDG02 programme 4.90 V in 14 of 18 samples (Type A), and the eAssist mild hybrid more than 4.65 V in 7 of 10 samples with the 12 V supply above 8.8 V (Type B).
s: MIL and service hybrid system message
Charging and regeneration limited
c: Sense lead S shorted to a higher cell or busbar
Measuring chip reading channel S incorrectly
Real overvoltage of the cell or block on channel S

P0B99.d: P0B99 is the erratic variant within the sense S group. A public manufacturer description does not exist.
s: Sporadic hybrid warning without a pattern
Code often stored as history, hard to reproduce
c: Fretting corrosion on the terminal of sense lead S
Cracked solder joint for channel S on the monitoring board
Harness chafing that only shorts under movement

P0B9A.d: P0B9A is the open-circuit code for sense T, the twentieth cell channel. GM uses it only on lithium-ion packs.
s: MIL, hybrid or EV system warning
Ready mode or charging blocked
c: Open sense lead T at the cell tab or connector
Poor busbar or splice joint in the channel T path
Monitoring board input for channel T failed

P0B9B.d: On the 2012 two-mode trucks sense T is block 20, the last of their twenty nickel-metal hydride blocks, and P0B9B shows how GM handles the missing neighbour: block 20 alone is multiplied by twenty and compared with the pack voltage, and a gap above 70 V in 160 of 170 samples sets the code as Type B. All other channels there use a pair of blocks.
s: MIL, drivability usually unchanged
Hybrid assist or EV range slightly reduced
c: Channel T measurement stuck or sluggish
Block 20 voltage diverging from pack voltage on two-mode NiMH packs
Faulty pack voltage reference used for the comparison

P0B9C.d: P0B9C signals that sense T reads too low. On the 2012 two-mode trucks this is block 20, and because no block 21 exists the low test there looks at block 20 alone: below 2 V in 15 of 20 samples, Type B, while channels R and S each need their upper neighbour to read low as well.
s: MIL and hybrid warning
Reduced power, engine may not shut off on hybrids
c: Sense lead T shorted to ground or a lower potential
Weak or discharged NiMH block 20 on two-mode packs
Failed measuring input for channel T

P0B9D.d: If sense T reports more voltage than its cell can hold, the battery controller stores P0B9D. GM documents it on several systems.
s: MIL and service hybrid or EV system message
Charging power reduced
c: Sense lead T shorted to a higher cell or busbar
Measuring input for channel T drifting high
Cell or block T genuinely overcharged

P0B9E.d: P0B9E would describe a sense T signal that flickers. It lacks any public manufacturer documentation.
s: Intermittent warning lamp
Occasional brief loss of electric drive
c: Loose or spread terminal in the channel T connector
Connection that opens with temperature changes
Electrical interference coupling into sense lead T

P0B9F.d: P0B9F covers an open or high-resistance sense U lead, channel twenty-one. From U onward the 2012 two-mode trucks drop out, as their pack has only twenty blocks, so this code is a lithium-ion matter at GM.
s: MIL and hybrid or EV system warning
No start or ready mode on some vehicles
Charging not possible
c: Sense lead U interrupted or detached from its cell
Corroded terminal raising the resistance of lead U
Fault in the balancing circuit used for the channel U test

P0BA0.d: P0BA0 tells the technician that channel U gives a number, but the number does not move with the pack. GM checks this rationality only on lithium-ion systems, since the two-mode NiMH trucks end at block 20.
s: MIL, often without driver-noticeable change
Electric range may be reduced
c: Measuring channel U holding a fixed value
Software or calibration issue in the battery controller
Cell U behaving differently from its neighbours due to ageing

P0BA1.d: P0BA1 is stored when sense U reads close to zero. GM's lithium-ion controllers of the 2016 Volt and ELR and of 2019 treat 0.2 V or less over 1.4 s in a 2 s window as a Type A fault, provided no open sense line, lost slave communication or balancing fault is already active.
s: MIL and EV or hybrid system warning
Propulsion power limited
c: Sense lead U shorted towards ground or a lower cell
Dead measuring input for channel U
Cell U internally shorted or deeply discharged

P0BA2.d: P0BA2 flags an excessive voltage on channel U. GM's eAssist mild hybrid uses the lowest threshold of the documented systems: above 4.65 V in 7 of 10 samples with the 12 V supply above 8.8 V, Type B.
s: MIL and hybrid or EV warning
Charging stopped early
c: Sense lead U in contact with a higher potential

P0BA3.d: Within the sense U group, P0BA3 is the slot for a signal that is present but unsteady. No manufacturer documents it publicly; GM, the only maker whose tables cover channel U in detail, uses P0B9F to P0BA2 and nothing more.
s: Warning lamp that comes and goes
Brief reduced-power events
c: Fatigued crimp on sense lead U
Loose fastener at the busbar tap of channel U
Vibration damage to the flexible printed circuit

P0BA4.d: P0BA4 reports an open or poorly connected sense V lead, the twenty-second channel and the last before W begins at P0BA9. GM's 2019 battery energy control module recognises it through seven cases, including 1.3 V between neighbouring cells, less than 36 mV with the balancing gate on and splice voltages above 0.1 or 0.5 V, with 0.8 s of failure in 1.6 s, Type A.
s: MIL and hybrid or EV system warning
Vehicle may not become ready to drive
Charging blocked
c: Broken or unplugged sense lead V
High-resistance splice or busbar joint on channel V
Cell monitoring board fault on channel V

P0BA5.d: P0BA5 describes a sense V value that stays within limits but fails a rationality check against the other cells. GM's 16OBDG02 programme demands a trend of at least 0.002 V in the same direction as the average whenever that average moves more than 0.022 V, with 35 failures in 40 evaluations giving Type A.
s: MIL, little change in driving
Reduced regeneration or assist possible
c: Channel V reading stuck while other cells move
Aged cell V responding differently to load

P0BA6.d: A sense V reading that collapses towards zero produces P0BA6. The threshold depends on the system: GM's eAssist mild hybrid uses under 1.4 V in 7 of 10 samples with at least 8.8 V on the 12 V side, Type B, while GM's lithium-ion battery controllers of 2016 and 2019 go down to 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s within 2 s, Type A.
s: MIL and service hybrid or EV system message
Power limited, restart may be refused
c: Sense lead V shorted to ground or a lower cell
Monitoring board input for channel V failed

P0BA7.d: P0BA7 is the high-voltage plausibility code for channel V. The battery controller compares the measured value against a ceiling no healthy cell should reach: 4.8 V for 1.4 s within 2 s in GM's 2016 Volt and ELR and in the 2019 battery energy control module (Type A), 4.90 V in 14 of 18 samples of 100 ms in the 16OBDG02 programme (Type A), and 4.65 V in 7 of 10 samples in the eAssist mild hybrid (Type B).
s: MIL and hybrid or EV warning
Charging and regeneration reduced
c: Sense lead V touching a higher cell tab or busbar
Measuring chip with faulty reference reading channel V high

P0BA8.d: P0BA8 completes the five codes of channel V and is meant for an unstable rather than a failed sense V signal. There is no public manufacturer documentation for it.
s: Occasional hybrid or EV warning
Fault not reproducible during short workshop test
c: Contact of lead V lost intermittently under vibration
Joint on channel V opening with thermal cycling
Corroded connector pin for channel V

P0BA9.d: P0BA9 opens the W group, the twenty-third cell voltage channel, and flags a sense lead that is open or badly connected. GM's 2019 battery energy control module checks seven cases, ranging from a reading under 36 mV while the balancing gate of that cell is switched on to at least 1.3 V between neighbouring cells and splice voltages above 0.1 V or 0.5 V at busbar joints; 0.8 s of failure within 1.6 s sets it as Type A.
s: MIL with hybrid or EV system warning
Reduced propulsion power or no ready mode
Charging interrupted or refused
c: Broken, chafed or unplugged sense lead W
High-resistance busbar or splice joint at channel W
Failed input on the cell monitoring board for W

P0BAA.d: Here the W reading is not missing but implausible: it fails to follow the rest of the pack. GM's 2019 hybrid powertrain control processor 2 watches for the average cell voltage to move more than 0.022 V between samples and then expects channel W to trend at least 0.005 V in the same direction; 35 failures in 40 samples at 100 ms give a Type A fault.
s: Warning lamp with little change in driving
Possibly limited regeneration or electric assist
c: Measuring input for W frozen at a fixed value
Battery controller software needing an update
Cell W reacting differently to load because of ageing

P0BAB.d: A W channel reading at or near zero sets P0BAB. How low is too low depends on the battery: GM's lithium-ion modules of 2016 and 2019 react to 0.2 V or less held for 1.4 s within a 2 s window, Type A, and the 16OBDG02 programme to under 0.20 V in 14 of 18 samples at 100 ms.
s: Hybrid or EV warning and MIL
Reduced power output
Charging limited or blocked
c: Sense lead W shorted to a lower cell potential
Measuring input for W on the monitoring board failed
Cell W deeply discharged or internally shorted

P0BAC.d: P0BAC is the upper counterpart to P0BAB: channel W reports more voltage than a single cell can plausibly hold. GM sets the limit at 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s within 2 s in the 2011 and 2016 Volt battery modules, which makes it a one-trip fault.
s: MIL and battery system warning
Charging and regeneration stopped
Possible reduced power mode
c: Sense lead W in contact with a higher cell potential
Monitoring board input for W reading too high
Cell W actually overcharged after a balancing fault

P0BAD.d: P0BAD is reserved for a W signal that drops out or jumps for short moments instead of failing outright. No manufacturer documents the code publicly.
s: Warning lamp that comes and goes
Occasional short power reduction
c: Loose or fretting connector pin on lead W
Crimp on lead W opening with temperature changes
Cracked solder joint on the monitoring board input W

P0BAE.d: Channel X, number twenty-four, starts with P0BAE, the open-lead code. The first-generation Volt of 2011 already detected it through several cases: two neighbouring readings more than 1 V apart, a busbar sense voltage above 0.7 V combined with an implausible cell voltage, or adjacent cells differing by more than 0.5 V on a shared supply line.
s: MIL and service message for the high-voltage system
Vehicle may stay out of ready mode
Charging stops early
c: Sense lead X broken or disconnected
Loose busbar fastener at the X sensing point
Sense harness X damaged during earlier battery work

P0BAF.d: P0BAF covers a sense X signal that is electrically present yet does not behave like a real cell. For model year 2016 GM documents two versions in the same booklet.
s: MIL without obvious driving change
Reduced electric range in some cases
c: Sense X value stuck while the pack voltage changes
Calibration of the battery controller requiring reprogramming
Cell X with deviating internal resistance

P0BB0.d: When channel X reads too low, P0BB0 is stored. In GM's eAssist mild hybrid the battery interface module sets it below 1.4 V in seven of ten samples at 200 ms, provided the 12 V system is above 8.8 V and the group fault P1B38 is not active, as a two-trip Type B fault.
s: Hybrid system warning and MIL
Electric assist or propulsion reduced
Charging not possible
c: Short between sense lead X and a lower potential
Defective measuring channel X in the monitoring electronics
Cell X collapsed or internally shorted

P0BB1.d: P0BB1 means the battery controller sees too much voltage on sense X. In GM's 2019 battery energy control module the threshold is 4.8 V or more, held for 1.4 s within a 2 s window, and the code is Type A, so the MIL comes on in the first trip.
s: MIL in the first trip
Charging and regenerative braking disabled
c: Sense lead X shorted to the next higher cell

P0BB2.d: Of the five X codes, P0BB2 is the only one without any public manufacturer description. It is intended for a sense X signal that flickers, drops out briefly or jumps between values.
s: Intermittent warning lamp
Sporadic hybrid system message
c: Contact on lead X opening under vibration
Moisture or corrosion in the X sense connector
Harness X chafing against the module housing

P0BB3.d: P0BB3 reports that the sense lead of channel Y, the twenty-fifth cell group, is no longer properly connected. GM's 16OBDG02 programme does not wait for odd voltages but calculates the resistance of the sense line and fails it above 30.00 in seven of nine samples, which is a one-trip Type A fault; the unit is missing in the table.
s: MIL and high-voltage system warning
Vehicle may not start in electric mode
Charging aborted
c: Open circuit in sense lead Y
Corroded or loose terminal raising line resistance at Y
Cell monitoring slave board fault on input Y

P0BB4.d: P0BB4 is a plausibility code: the controller compares how the Y reading changes over time with the behaviour of all other cells. In the 16OBDG02 programme a sample counts as failed when the pack average moves by more than 0.022 V but Y has not trended at least 0.002 V the same way; 35 such results in 40 evaluations set a one-trip Type A fault.
s: MIL, vehicle still drivable
Battery power occasionally limited
c: Analogue input Y frozen at one value
Weak cell Y with sluggish voltage response

P0BB5.d: P0BB5 stands for a sense Y voltage below the plausible minimum. GM's 2016 Volt module and the 2019 battery energy control module both use 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s inside a 2 s window and flag it as Type A.
s: Hybrid or EV warning with MIL
Noticeably reduced power
c: Pinched sense wire Y shorting to a lower potential

P0BB6.d: The battery controller logs P0BB6 when the Y channel climbs above a level no healthy cell reaches. GM's first Volt of 2011 put that limit at 4.8 V or more, 1.4 s within 2 s, with the MIL after one trip.
s: MIL and charging stopped
Regeneration disabled
c: Sense input Y bridged to the next cell potential
Defective input Y on the monitoring board
Overcharged cell Y after a balancing problem

P0BB7.d: P0BB7 would describe an unstable sense Y signal, one that is mostly correct but drops out or jumps from time to time. No manufacturer publishes a monitor for it.
s: Warning lamp appears now and then
Short-lived power limitation
c: Intermittent contact in the Y sense connector
Crimp or weld on lead Y opening when hot
Hairline crack in a solder joint of input Y

P0BB8.d: P0BB8 is the open-circuit code of channel Z, the twenty-sixth and last cell channel with a generic P0 code. GM packs with more channels continue with manufacturer codes, for example P1B28 for the circuit of AA in the 2019 tables.
s: MIL and stop or service warning for the drive system
Ready mode may be refused
No charging
c: Excessive resistance at the splice or busbar of Z

P0BB9.d: With P0BB9 the controller says that sense Z does not track the pack: the value is within limits, but it stays still or moves the wrong way while the other cells change. GM's 2019 hybrid powertrain control processor 2 enables the comparison once the system voltage is above 10.20 V and the average cell voltage shifts by more than 0.022 V, then demands a trend of at least 0.005 V on Z; 35 failures in 40 samples are Type
s: MIL, driving largely unaffected
Possibly lower assist or regeneration
c: Z reading static despite changing pack voltage
Monitoring board or controller calibration fault
Cell Z with abnormal charge and discharge behaviour

P0BBA.d: P0BBA is stored when the voltage measured on channel Z falls below the lower limit. In the 16OBDG02 programme the hybrid processor checks Z every 100 ms and fails it below 0.20 V in 14 of 18 samples, a Type A fault, but only with a system voltage above 10.20 V and no open-circuit fault on the cell.
s: MIL and hybrid or EV warning
Limited power and charging
c: Short in the Z sense wiring or connector
Failed channel Z on the monitoring board

P0BBB.d: If the Z channel shows a cell voltage above the upper limit, the controller sets P0BBB. The 2016 Volt battery module uses 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s in a 2 s window, Type A, and checks first that the cell monitoring slave is communicating and no open sense line is reported.
s: MIL and charging stopped
Reduced regeneration
c: Sense lead Z shorted towards the higher neighbour cell

P0BBC.d: P0BBC closes the generic block of 26 cell voltage channels from A to Z; after it J2012 moves on to pack-level codes such as P0BBD and P0BBE. The code is meant for a Z signal that is unstable rather than absent.
s: Warning lamp appearing irregularly
Occasional brief loss of electric drive power
c: Intermittent contact on sense lead Z
Joint at channel Z opening with heat cycling
Corrosion in the Z sense connector

P0BBD.d: P0BBD means the spread between cells or blocks of the pack has grown beyond what the controller accepts. GM used it on the two-mode hybrids, where a difference of more than 1.5 V between adjacent block voltages in three of three samples at 1 s, with battery current above 0.2 A, set a Type B fault labelled as end-of-life deviation.
s: MIL or electrical system warning
Reduced propulsion power and capped state of charge
Reduced electric range
Drive system cannot be activated in severe cases
c: Cells or modules with increased self-discharge or capacity loss
Controller software or cell capacity adaptation needing an update
Aged battery pack at end of life
Cell balancing unable to equalise the pack

P0BBE.d: P0BBE watches the gap between the highest and the lowest cell voltage in the pack. GM's first-generation Volt sets it when that difference exceeds 0.3 V in 50 of 245 samples taken every 100 ms, provided the cell voltage rationality fault is not active; it is a one-trip Type A fault.
s: MIL and hybrid system warning
Reduced electric range or propulsion
Vehicle may not start
c: Cells drifted apart beyond what balancing can correct
Battery pack control module software needing an update
Defective or aged high-voltage battery pack
Faulty cell voltage measurement simulating a spread

P0BBF.d: Air-cooled hybrid packs draw cooling air through a 12 V blower that is fed through a fuse and often a relay; the controller watches the voltage reaching the fan, and Toyota even uses that measured supply voltage to correct the fan duty. P0BBF means this feed is open or missing while the fan should be powered.
s: Hybrid system warning or MIL on
Battery fan silent when it should run
Reduced electric assist in hot weather or under load
c: Blown fuse in the battery fan feed
Fan relay contacts not closing or relay coil open
Open supply wire or loose terminal at the fan connector

P0BC0.d: P0BC0 reports that the voltage feeding the battery cooling fan is lower than expected while the fan is switched on. A short to ground downstream of the fuse, a corroded connector or a relay with burnt contacts drops the voltage, so the fan turns slowly or not at all.
s: Hybrid system warning or MIL on
Battery fan runs slowly or noticeably weaker
Reduced electric assist when the pack is warm
c: Fan supply wire chafed and shorted to ground
Burnt fan relay contacts or corroded terminals causing voltage drop
Weak 12 V auxiliary battery or poor ground
Seizing fan motor pulling excessive current

P0BC1.d: P0BC1 flags voltage on the battery fan feed when there should be none, or more than expected. GM documents it for the battery pack control module of its Two-Mode hybrid SUVs and pickups (Tahoe, Yukon, Escalade, Silverado, Sierra; 2012 and 2013 tables) as a welded fan relay: with the fan commanded off, a fan monitor voltage of at least 0.9 V in 10 of 20 samples at 100 ms sets it, provided the 12 V system is between 9
s: MIL on after two trips
Battery fan keeps running after the vehicle is switched off
Discharged 12 V battery after standing
c: Fan feed shorted to a constant battery voltage wire
Relay control output in the module stuck on

P0BC2.d: Battery temperature sensor E is the fifth thermistor in the high-voltage pack; GM's Chevrolet Volt bulletin 18-NA-342 lists the E codes as temperature sensor 5 of nine. P0BC2 is the general circuit code, used when the controller detects an electrical fault without classing it as low, high or erratic.
s: Hybrid or EV system warning and MIL
Reduced power or charging rate
Battery cooling running more than usual
c: Loose or corroded connector of sensor E at the sensing board
Faulty input on the battery sensing board or module

P0BC3.d: P0BC3 is the plausibility check for battery temperature sensor E, GM's sensor 5: its reading is compared with the other pack sensors, which should agree closely. GM's 2016 hybrid table fails it when E is more than 25 °C away from the average of the others in 50 of 67 samples; the 2018 CT6 plug-in table more than 20 °C for 5 s within 6.7 s; the eAssist mild hybrid (13OBDG05C) allows only 8.55 °C, and only after the mo
s: MIL on after two trips
Battery too cold or reduced power message
Limited charge and discharge power
c: Sensor E drifting or poorly seated on its cell group
Module software setting the code falsely in the cold (GM Volt)
Real local hot spot from a weak cell group or blocked airflow

P0BC4.d: Sensor E is an NTC thermistor with a pull-up resistor, so its voltage falls as it gets hotter; a short to ground therefore looks like an extremely hot cell group. GM's 2016 table sets P0BC4 when the converted value exceeds 160 °C in 8 of 10 samples; the 2011 Volt table and GM's 2019 battery module table use above 87.5 °C for 1.4 s within 2 s; the eAssist mild hybrid flags a sense voltage under 0.3 V, about 90 °C, in
s: MIL on after two trips
Implausibly high temperature for sensor E on the scan tool
Reduced power and battery fan or cooling at full speed
c: Sensor E signal wire shorted to ground inside the pack
Moisture or contamination on the sensing board

P0BC5.d: P0BC5 reports that battery temperature sensor E delivers a voltage above its valid range. With GM's NTC sensors that reads as extreme cold, pointing to an open wire, a backed-out pin at the sensing board or a cracked thermistor.
s: MIL on after two trips
Battery too cold, plug in to warm message
Very limited power or charging
c: Open sensor E wire or backed-out pin at the sensing board
Module software misreading in the cold (GM Volt, reprogramming)

P0BC6.d: P0BC6 flags erratic behaviour of battery temperature sensor E: the reading jumps far faster than the heavy battery mass could warm or cool. GM documents the method in its 2016 and 2018 hybrid tables (16OBDG02, 18OBDG02).
s: MIL on after two trips
Sensor E value jumping on the scan tool
Occasional power reduction
c: Loose terminal or unlatched connector of sensor E
Cracked or chafed sensor wire breaking contact intermittently
Sensing board fault affecting several temperature inputs

P0BC7.d: Many battery cooling fans report their actual speed back to the controller as a pulse signal; Toyota patents describe a rotation sensor on the fan motor whose measured speed is compared with the target. P0BC7 means this feedback line for fan 1 is open or carries no usable signal.
s: Hybrid system warning or MIL on
Reduced electric assist or charging power
Fan audible even though the code reports no feedback
c: Open feedback wire or loose pin at the fan connector
Failed speed sensor or electronics inside the fan unit
Faulty feedback input in the controlling module

P0BC8.d: P0BC8 compares the speed fed back by battery cooling fan 1 with what the controller commanded. GM's 2016 and 2018 hybrid tables run two checks.
s: MIL on after two trips
Weak airflow or unusual fan noise from the battery intake
Reduced electric assist when the pack warms up
c: Dust-clogged impeller, blocked intake or worn fan bearing
Fan keeps running while commanded off (stuck drive or relay)
Fan electronics reporting a wrong speed

P0BC9.d: P0BC9 means the speed feedback of battery cooling fan 1 is implausibly low while the fan is running. GM evaluates the feedback as a frequency: in its 2016 and 2018 hybrid tables the code counts a failure when the frequency stays below 8 Hz with the fan enabled at 11 to 89 % duty for more than 8 s and system voltage above 10.2 V; 16 failures in 20 samples at 250 ms set it as Type B, two trips.
s: MIL on after two trips
No airflow from the battery cooling fan
Reduced power when the battery gets warm
c: Fan seized, blocked or without power
Feedback wire shorted to ground or interrupted
Failed speed sensor inside the fan unit

P0BCA.d: P0BCA means the speed feedback of battery cooling fan 1 is implausibly high. GM's 2016 and 2018 hybrid tables count a failure when the feedback frequency exceeds 290 Hz with the fan enabled at 11 to 89 % duty for more than 8 s and system voltage above 10.2 V; 16 failures in 20 samples at 250 ms set it as Type B, two trips.
s: MIL on after two trips
Implausible fan speed reading on the scan tool
Possible power reduction
c: Electrical noise on the feedback line from poor routing or a bad ground
Feedback wire shorted to voltage or another signal
Fan electronics sending an invalid speed signal

P0BCB.d: P0BCB flags a speed feedback from battery cooling fan 1 that drops out or jumps in a way no rotating fan can, typically a loose contact in the feedback line. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; GM's 2016 and 2018 hybrid tables, which watch the same pulse feedback, list only performance, low and high (P0BC8, P0BC9, P0BCA).
s: Hybrid system warning or MIL, sometimes coming and going
Fan speed reading jumping on the scan tool
Occasional power reduction
c: Loose or corroded terminal in the feedback circuit
Chafed harness near the fan or battery case
Intermittent fault in the fan's speed sensor

P0BCC.d: In a two-machine hybrid one inverter feeds the traction motor and a second one the generator, the machine that is mainly driven by the engine to charge the battery or start it. Its power switches carry thermistors so the controller can cut current before they overheat.
s: Hybrid system warning or check engine lamp
Reduced generator output and battery charging
Engine runs more often or hybrid mode limited
c: Fault of the sensor or its circuit inside the inverter assembly
Loose or corroded connector at the inverter
Software fault in the inverter or hybrid control module

P0BCD.d: P0BCD flags a generator inverter temperature sensor A whose signal is electrically valid but does not fit the operating state, for example a value stuck at one temperature or far from the other temperatures after a long soak. Ford documents this exact code: on 2020 Lincoln Aviator 3.0L hybrids built up to 18 July 2020, P0BCD stored in the inverter system controller (SOBDMC) lights the MIL and is caused by software; t
s: Malfunction indicator lamp
Often no noticeable change in driving
Hybrid system warning message possible
c: Inverter controller software (Ford SSM 49120, Lincoln Aviator 2020)
Sensor drifting or stuck at one value
Uneven inverter coolant flow distorting the comparison

P0BCE.d: P0BCE means the signal of generator inverter temperature sensor A is below its valid range. Inverter thermistors are usually NTC types with a pull-up resistor, as GM's tables describe for the drive motor inverter sensors: a short to ground or a shorted element pulls the voltage down, which the controller reads as an impossibly hot inverter.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Generator power strongly limited
Battery charge drops, engine runs more
c: Shorted sensor or circuit inside the inverter assembly
Signal shorted to ground in external wiring, where present
Moisture or coolant inside the inverter housing

P0BCF.d: P0BCF reports a signal from generator inverter temperature sensor A above its valid range. With the usual NTC thermistor and pull-up, an open circuit, a lost sensor ground or a cracked element drives the voltage up, which reads as an extremely cold inverter.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced generator output
Implausibly low inverter temperature in live data
c: Open sensor or circuit inside the inverter assembly
Loose, corroded or unplugged connector at the inverter

P0BD0.d: P0BD0 is reserved for a generator inverter temperature sensor A signal that jumps or briefly drops out instead of failing for good. A liquid-cooled inverter changes temperature slowly, so sudden steps point to a contact problem or to interference: a Hitachi patent on inverter systems explains that the small sensor signal can pick up noise from the high-voltage main circuit and has to be filtered statistically.
s: Warning lamp that comes and goes
Brief drops in generator or hybrid power
Jumping inverter temperature in live data
c: Loose or corroded contact at the inverter connector
Intermittent fault inside the inverter assembly
Interference from the high-voltage circuit on the sensor signal

P0BD1.d: Which thermistor is called sensor C depends on the maker. In GM's hybrid tables it is the second sensor of the motor A inverter: the phase V sensor in the 2016 to 2019 tables, labelled temperature sensor 2 in the Volt and ELR.
s: Hybrid system warning or check engine lamp
Reduced electric drive power
Possible loss of electric drive
c: Internal fault of the sensor inside the power inverter module
Corroded or loose connector at the inverter module
Software fault in the motor control processor

P0BD2.d: P0BD2 checks whether inverter temperature sensor C, GM's second sensor in the motor A inverter, agrees with the other temperatures after a cold soak. More than 20 °C apart sets it: Type B, two trips, on the 2016 Volt; Type A in a 2019 table; Type A on the 2011 Volt and 2016 ELR, compared with coolant and transmission temperature after 6 h off.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp, often without drivability change
Propulsion power reduced message (Bolt EV)
Red hybrid warning in the cluster (Porsche)
c: Inverter module software (GM bulletin 18-NA-064, Bolt EV/Ampera-e)
Sticking thermostat in the power electronics coolant hose (Porsche Cayenne S E-Hybrid)
Inverter temperature sensor C drifting out of tolerance

P0BD3.d: P0BD3 means the signal of inverter temperature sensor C, the phase V sensor of GM's motor A inverter, is below its valid range. GM uses an NTC thermistor with a pull-up on the sensing board, so a short to ground reads as an impossibly hot inverter.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Drive motor power strongly limited
Reduced regeneration
c: Shorted sensor or circuit inside the power inverter module
Sensor signal shorted to ground in external wiring, where present
Moisture or coolant inside the inverter housing

P0BD4.d: P0BD4 reports a voltage from inverter temperature sensor C above its valid range. For GM's NTC sensor this is an implausibly cold inverter, typically caused by an open circuit, a lost ground or a cracked element.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp, depending on model after two trips
Reduced electric drive power
Implausibly low inverter temperature in live data
c: Open sensor or circuit inside the power inverter module
Loose, corroded or unplugged connector at the inverter

P0BD5.d: P0BD5 is meant for an inverter temperature sensor C signal that jumps or drops out for short moments. Because the heat sink of a liquid-cooled inverter changes temperature smoothly, sudden steps point to a contact fault or to interference; a Hitachi patent explains that the small thermistor signal can pick up noise from the high-voltage main circuit.
s: Warning lamp that comes and goes
Brief power reductions while driving
Jumping inverter temperature in live data
c: Loose or corroded contact at the inverter module
Intermittent fault inside the power inverter module
Interference from the high-voltage circuit on the sensor signal

P0BD6.d: Sensor D is, in GM's hybrid tables, the second thermistor of the motor B inverter, the counterpart of sensor C in the motor A inverter: phase V in the 2016 to 2019 tables, temperature sensor 2 of inverter B on the Volt. Other makers assign the letter differently.
s: Hybrid system warning or check engine lamp
Reduced electric drive or generator power
Higher fuel consumption in hybrid operation
c: Internal fault of the sensor inside the power inverter module
Corroded or loose connector at the inverter module
Software fault in the motor control processor

P0BD7.d: P0BD7 is the plausibility check for inverter temperature sensor D, GM's second sensor in the motor B inverter. After a cold soak its reading is compared with an average vehicle temperature; more than 20 °C apart sets the code, Type B, two trips, on the 2016 Volt and Type A in a 2019 table.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp, often after two trips
Often no noticeable drivability change
Further inverter temperature codes may be stored
c: Inverter temperature sensor D drifting out of tolerance
Uneven inverter coolant flow after soak

P0BD8.d: P0BD8 means the signal of inverter temperature sensor D is below its valid range; with an NTC thermistor and pull-up that reads as an extremely hot inverter, usually from a short to ground or an internal sensor fault. GM sets it above 170 °C for 2.5 of 3.5 s, Type B, two trips, on the 2016 Volt, above 159 °C, Type A, in a 2019 table, above 130 °C, Type A, on the 2011 Volt and above 125 °C, two trips, in the 2012 tabl
s: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Vehicle does not start, Electric Traction System Fault (Jeep)
Electric drive power strongly limited
c: Shorted sensor or circuit inside the inverter (Jeep Compass PHEV bulletin)
Sensor signal shorted to ground in external wiring, where present
Moisture or coolant inside the inverter housing

P0BD9.d: P0BD9 means inverter temperature sensor D delivers a voltage above its valid range. For GM's NTC sensor in the motor B inverter that equals an implausibly cold inverter, so an open circuit, a lost ground or a cracked thermistor is likely.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp, depending on model after two trips
Reduced motor B power and regeneration
Implausibly low inverter temperature in live data
c: Open sensor or circuit inside the power inverter module
Loose, corroded or unplugged connector at the inverter

P0BDA.d: P0BDA covers an inverter temperature sensor D signal that changes in steps or drops out briefly. Real temperatures of a liquid-cooled inverter move smoothly, so such jumps suggest a contact problem or interference from the high-voltage switching, which a Hitachi patent on inverter systems names as a typical disturbance of the small sensor signal.
s: Warning lamp that comes and goes
Brief power reductions while driving
Jumping inverter temperature in live data
c: Loose or corroded contact at the inverter module
Intermittent fault inside the power inverter module
Interference from the high-voltage circuit on the sensor signal

P0BDB.d: Which thermistor counts as inverter temperature sensor E is set by the manufacturer. In GM's hybrid tables it is the third sensor of the motor A inverter (PIM sensor #3), assigned to phase W in the 2016 to 2019 tables.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp or hybrid system warning
Reduced electric drive power
Further inverter temperature codes stored at the same time
c: Internal fault of the thermistor or its circuit inside the power inverter module
Corroded or loose connector at the inverter module
Software fault in the motor control processor

P0BDC.d: P0BDC checks whether inverter temperature sensor E, GM's phase W sensor in the motor A inverter, agrees with the vehicle after a long stand. The 2016 and 2018 tables compare it after a cold soak with a calculated average temperature; more than 20 °C apart for 0.525 of 0.625 s sets Type B, two trips.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp after two drives, often without any drivability change
Code found during inspection without customer complaint

Uneven inverter cooling or residual heat after the soak period
Failing power inverter module (replace only with P0AC4 per GM PIC6303A)

P0BDD.d: P0BDD reports that the signal of inverter temperature sensor E, the phase W thermistor of GM's motor A inverter, sits below its valid range. GM uses an NTC thermistor with a pull-up on the sensing board, so a short to ground appears as an impossibly hot inverter.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Drive motor A power strongly limited
Reduced regenerative braking
c: Shorted thermistor or signal line inside the power inverter module
Signal shorted to ground in external wiring, where the design has any
Moisture or coolant inside the inverter housing

P0BDE.d: P0BDE means the signal of inverter temperature sensor E is above its valid range. For GM's NTC thermistor with pull-up that reads as an extremely cold phase W in the motor A inverter, typically an open circuit, lost reference ground or a failed sensor.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced electric drive power once the inverter has warmed up
c: Open thermistor or broken connection inside the power inverter module
Loose or corroded connector at the inverter
Lost sensor reference ground on the sensing board

P0BDF.d: P0BDF flags an unstable signal from inverter temperature sensor E: the reading jumps or drops out briefly instead of staying out of range, typically from a loose connector, a cracked solder joint or an ageing thermistor. In GM's hybrid tables sensor E is the phase W sensor of the motor A inverter, but GM does not list this erratic code; no manufacturer documents P0BDF publicly.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp that comes and goes
Occasional loss of electric drive power
c: Loose, corroded or vibrating connector at the inverter
Cracked solder joint on the inverter sensing board

P0BE0.d: Sensor F is, in GM's hybrid tables, the third thermistor of the motor B inverter (inverter B sensor #3), the counterpart of sensor E in the motor A inverter; the 2016 to 2019 tables assign it to phase W. Other makers may use the letter differently.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp or hybrid system warning
Reduced power from drive motor B
Higher fuel consumption in hybrid operation

Corroded or loose connector at the inverter module
Software fault in the motor control processor

P0BE1.d: P0BE1 is the plausibility check of inverter temperature sensor F, GM's phase W thermistor in the motor B inverter. After the car has stood long enough, its reading must match a reference: in the 2016 and 2018 tables a calculated average after cold soak, with more than 20 °C difference for 0.525 of 0.625 s setting Type B over two trips, Type A in a 2019 table.

Code found during inspection without customer complaint

Uneven inverter cooling or residual heat after the soak period

P0BE2.d: P0BE2 is set when the voltage from inverter temperature sensor F, the phase W thermistor in GM's motor B inverter, drops below the valid window. Because GM pairs an NTC element with a pull-up resistor, a short to ground is converted into a temperature far above anything the inverter can survive.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Power of drive motor B strongly limited
Engine runs more often in hybrid operation

Signal shorted to ground in external wiring, where the design has any
Moisture or coolant inside the inverter housing

P0BE3.d: P0BE3 is the high-signal fault of inverter temperature sensor F, GM's phase W thermistor in the motor B inverter. With an NTC element and pull-up, an open circuit or a sensor that has lost ground drives the voltage up, which the controller reads as an implausibly cold inverter.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced power from drive motor B once warmed up

Loose or corroded connector at the inverter
Lost sensor reference ground on the sensing board

P0BE4.d: P0BE4 stands for brief dropouts or jumps in the signal of inverter temperature sensor F, which GM's hybrid tables place at phase W of the motor B inverter. The reading returns to normal between events, which separates it from the steady low and high faults P0BE2 and P0BE3.

P0BE5.d: The inverter of drive motor A measures the current in each motor phase with a current sensor; the controller needs these values for torque control and overcurrent protection. P0BE5 is the general circuit code for the phase U sensor, used for an electrical fault that is not classed as offset, low or high.
s: Hybrid system warning and malfunction indicator lamp
Reduced power from drive motor A
Possible loss of electric drive

Supply or signal fault on the inverter's sensor board
Software fault in the motor control processor

P0BE6.d: GM uses P0BE6 as the offset check of the phase U current sensor in the motor A inverter. Turtle (limp home) light and Service 4WD light (Jeep)
Reduced electric drive power
c: Zero offset of the phase U current sensor drifted beyond the limit
Faulty sensing electronics in the power inverter module
